nodes.NAME: outputagprotect
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Agricultural output protection portion.  A value of 1 translates on the full efect of scenarios affecting Agricultural output, and a 0 no effect, you can use partial values between 0 and 1.

nodes.NAME: outputenprotect
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy output protection portion.  A value of 1 translates on the full efect of scenarios affecting Agricultural output, and a 0 no effect, you can use partial values between 0 and 1.

nodes.NAME: hhsaveneedrat
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Allows the user to create an initial discrepancy between accumulated savings (HHSAVSTOCK) and integrated need (HHSAVNEEDSTOCK).

nodes.NAME: actreaon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Action-reaction switch.  A value of 1 (as in the base case) turns on an action-reaction dynamic in the determination of threat.  A value of 0 turns it off.

nodes.NAME: edqualag15m
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education quality, adult 15+ score, multiplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: workageentry
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Age of common entry into the work force, sets the entry to the labor force.

nodes.NAME: ageofmarriagetfrelas
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Responsiveness of TFR to changes in average age of marriage From expected value, i.e., base case forecast. A value of .01 will decrease TFR by .01 when age of marriage is one year more than the base case forecast.

nodes.NAME: ageofmarriagem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The rate of change for age of marriage impacted by a multliplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: workageretire
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Age of normal retirement, sets the exit of the labor force

nodes.NAME: workageretiresv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Age of retirement to compute savings rate, input for function to compute Savings rate needed, it allows to analyze Savings rate needed independently of changes in retirement age when using mixed scenarios.

nodes.NAME: envylchgadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Global additive shift factor for the annual change in agricultural yield by country/region.

nodes.NAME: envylchgm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for the annual change in agricultural yield by country/region.

nodes.NAME: agconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Agriculture demand convergence time, represents the time required  for agricultural demand to converge to the function's predicted values, in years. Initial country data may deviate From cross-sectional predictions due to possible data errors or unique country factors. This parameter assumes that over time, such discrepancies will align with the predicted values. A high value like 10000 stops convergence; a low value like 10 speeds it up.

nodes.NAME: agxvaluem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Billion $ Value of agricultural exports, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase exports and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: agxm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on agricultural exports, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase investment and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: agmvaluem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Billion $ Value of agricultural imports, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase imports and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: agmm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on agricultural imports, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase investment and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: inputagrim
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Agricultural input multiplier.  A multiplier on the use of agricultural products as inputs in all economic sectors, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase material input and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: aginvm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on agriculture investment, by region and without units. A value of 1 indicates no change. Values greater than 1 increase investment proportionally, and values less than 1 decrease it. Avoid changing the initial year value; instead, adjust the multiplier over time.

nodes.NAME: eliasp2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of agricultural investment in land to changes in economic return.  Eliasp1 and eliasp2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: eliasp1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of agricultural investment in land to economic return.  Eliasp1 and eliasp2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: aglossprodm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on agricultural production losses adjusts the proportion of food production lost at the point of production (for example, to pests in the field.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: agstkadjsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Agricultural stock change switch eliminates the impact of supply and demand imbalances on agricultural food stocks.  A value of 1 turns on the switch for highly specialized scenarios.

nodes.NAME: agtrdadjsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Agricultural trade switch eliminates the impact of domestic and international food stocks changes on trade ratios. A value of 1 turns on the switch for highly specialized scenarios.

nodes.NAME: aglosstransm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on agricultural transfer/distriction losses adjusts the proportion of food transfer lost at the point of transfer.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: elfdpr2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of yield to changes in stocks/inventories.  Elfdpr1 and elfdpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elfdpr1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of yield to stocks/inventories.  Elfdpr1 and elfdpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: ylmaxgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that roughly controls the the maximum increase in agricultural yields (.05 would be 5% annually).  It is phased downward at the hhighest values of current yields.

nodes.NAME: ylm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on agricultureal yields, by region. It is used to represent potential yield changes due to technological or environmental factors. The value is typically adjusted over time rather than in the initial year. For example, a value of 1 represents no change, 1.25 represents a 25 percent increase and .75 represents a 25 percent decrease.

nodes.NAME: agon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Agriculture switch turns on or off the linkages  between the agricultural submodel and all others, including economy. A value of 1 turns the linkages on; 0 turns them off. Useful for isolating submodels during analysis. Typically set to 1.

nodes.NAME: aiddon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Aid (foreign) donations as % of GDP.  A coefficient of foreign assistance, by country/region.  It is in percentage form and is the percentage of GDP given in foreign aid (e.g., -0.2 equals 0.2 percent of GDP).

nodes.NAME: aidgradpoint
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on aid received..  The model will allocate available aid so that all recipients receive aid proportional to specified targets, not necessarily equal to those targets.

nodes.NAME: aidlpm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Aid, loan portio multiplier.  This multiplier interacts with the coefficient that determines the portion of foreign aid that actually constitutes loans.

nodes.NAME: aidrecadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor on aid received.  The model will allocate available aid so that all recipients receive aid proportional to specified targets, not necessarily equal to those targets.

nodes.NAME: aidrecgovconp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Aid, share of aid received that is disbursed towards government consumption spending (the rest is used as transfer).

nodes.NAME: aidrecm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on aid received..  The model will allocate available aid so that all recipients receive aid proportional to specified targets, not necessarily equal to those targets.

nodes.NAME: AIDSDRATE
nodes.Parameter Explanation: AIDS death rate as % of HIV infection rate.  This refers to the percentage of infected individuals in a population who die in a given year, not to the percentage who ultimately die of AIDS.

nodes.NAME: aidsdratem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on AIDS death rate as a percentage of HIV infection rate. It refers to the percentage of infected individuals in a population who die in a given year, not to the percentage who ultimately die of AIDS.

nodes.NAME: aidsdrtadvr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the technical advance rate in control of deaths From those with AIDS. For example, anti-viral therapies.

nodes.NAME: ally
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Alliance membership switch.  A value of 1 indicates membership in the acting alliance and a value of 2 indicates membership in the reacting alliance (either alliance can consist of a single country or region).  Alliances can form or dissolve over time; membership in alliances can change.  None of that will, however, happen endogenously; you must specify alliance structures.  Alliance membership only affects war damage, not threat levels or war outbreak.

nodes.NAME: hllongvtyalpharatio
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Ratio parameter that controls the target Alpha coeficient.

nodes.NAME: hllongvtyalpha
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Alpha coeficient that controls how late does the mortality function kicks in (higher values make it kick in earlier).

nodes.NAME: druguseamphetaminem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the use of amphetamine drug.

nodes.NAME: ENVPRCHG
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The average annual precipitation change From 1990 by country/region

nodes.NAME: ENVTEMP
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The average annual temperature by country/region

nodes.NAME: ENVTPCHG
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The average annual temperature change From 1990 by country/region

nodes.NAME: femshrgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Annual growth rate of the female share in the labor force, expressed in percentage terms.

nodes.NAME: ENVYLCHG
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The annual change in agricultural yield by country/region

nodes.NAME: AQUACUL
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Aquaculture, in million metric tons, by region.  Users can provide assumptions over time about domestic fish production with this parameter.

nodes.NAME: aquaculgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial annual growth rate for aquaculture production (freshwater or marine) by region, expressed as a percentage. Avoid changing after the initial year; use a multiplier instead.

nodes.NAME: aquaculm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on aquaculture production, without units, by region. A value of 1 indicates no change; higher values increase demand, and lower values decrease it. Maintain the initial year's value, gradually adjusting the multiplier thereafter.

nodes.NAME: aquaculconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Aquaculture growth rate convergence time represents the time for  aquaculture growth rates to converge to zero, in years.

nodes.NAME: xarmsadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Arms exports additive factor.  A value of 0 implies no change, while positive values increase the underlying value and negative values decrease it.  Like other additive factors, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the parameter value over time.

nodes.NAME: xarmsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Arms exports multiplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: marmsadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Arms imports additive factor.  A value of 0 implies no change, while positive values increase the underlying value and negative values decrease it.  Like other additive factors, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the parameter value over time.

nodes.NAME: marmsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Arms imports multiplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: aimachiqm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Artificial Inteligence Machine IQ.

nodes.NAME: aitaskm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Artificial Inteligence Index for Specific Tasks.

nodes.NAME: co2perm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on atmospheric percentage of CO2.

nodes.NAME: sanithhlifepitlatrinebasic
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, sanitation, basic pit latrine, lifetime in years

nodes.NAME: hlbednetsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on availability of bednet. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hllongvtybetaratio
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Ratio parameter that controls the target Beta coeficient.

nodes.NAME: hllongvtybeta
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Beta coeficient that controls the shape of the mortality function (higher values make it steep, 0 makes it flat at 0, 1 makes it flat at 1).

nodes.NAME: bilateralsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to compute bilateral variables.

nodes.NAME: threatconstsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch used to select mode (0) all variables active, (1) constant trade share, (2)....

nodes.NAME: bilateraltradeforwardlinksw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to compute forward linkages From bilateral trade.

nodes.NAME: threattradesw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Used alongside threatconstsw to handle which trade sectors are held constant. 0 uses in-year values for all sectors, 1 keeps all sectors as a %GDP constant for THREAT calculations, and 2 does the same for all sectors.

nodes.NAME: hlbmim
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on body mass index.

nodes.NAME: ictbroadfromtelem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for proportion of fixed telephone divestment that is used for fixed broadband

nodes.NAME: wtempadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that sets the additive factor to the calculated global temperature.

nodes.NAME: clpcm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on per capita calorie demand, by region and without units. A value of 1 indicates no change; higher values increase demand, and lower values decrease it. Avoid changing the initial year's value; instead, adjust the multiplier over time.

nodes.NAME: clnf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Calorie need factor or multiplier on calorie needs, by region. Usually set at 1. It adjusts regional calorie requirements to address food shortages impacting infant mortality. A value of 0 turns off the feedback between food shortages and infant mortality for a region.

nodes.NAME: clsexp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Exponent parameter that links calorie shortage to starvation. Higher values lower starvation and lower values increase starvation.

nodes.NAME: calmax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Maximum kilocalories needed per person per day. This biologically determined value should generally not change over time.

nodes.NAME: clpccvm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on coefficient of variation (Std. Dev/Mean) for calories per capita.

nodes.NAME: clpccvr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for the Calories per Capita Coefficient of Variation: 0 for endogenous multivariate drivers, 1 for constant, 2 for median with GDPPC only, 3 for optimistic with GDPPC only, and 4 for pessimistic with GDPPC only

nodes.NAME: clpcmderm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for the Calories per Capita Minimum Dietary Energy Requirement.

nodes.NAME: clpcexovals
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Exogenous values for Calories per Capita; set to -100 to turn off.

nodes.NAME: calmeatm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Maximum proportion of calories From meat, increasing with income up to this cap. The value, between 0 and 1, is typically set only in the first year.

nodes.NAME: elcaput2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of capacity utilization to stock level change.  Elcaput1 and elcaput2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elcaput1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of capacity utilization to stock level.  Elcaput1 and elcaput2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: qem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Capital output ratio for energy multiplier.  A multiplier on all types of energy capital output, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the amount of capital required per unit of energy output and lower values decrease it. Lower this parameter gradually over time to simulate a decreased cost of an energy form (such as renewable energy) as a result of technological advance.  Raise it over time to simulate the addition to the capital cost of an energy form (say nuclear) as a result of the addition to those costs of environmental ones.

nodes.NAME: qeunconm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Capital output ratio for unconventional energy multiplier.  A multiplier on all types of energy capital output, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the amount of capital required per unit of energy output and lower values decrease it. Lower this parameter gradually over time to simulate a decreased cost of an energy form (such as renewable energy) as a result of technological advance.  Raise it over time to simulate the addition to the capital cost of an energy form (say nuclear) as a result of the addition to those costs of environmental ones.

nodes.NAME: keqshr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Share of capital equipment (K) in fixed capital.

nodes.NAME: ksadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on capital stocks. This parameter is primarily used to represent destruction of capital stocks due to conflict in a scenario. Care must be used with positive values to avoid increasing capital stocks without accounting for the associated trade-offs.

nodes.NAME: ksm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on capital stocks. This parameter is primarily used to represent destruction of capital stocks due to conflict in a scenario. Care must be used with positive values to avoid increasing capital stocks without accounting for the associated trade-offs.

nodes.NAME: QE(Oil)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Capital output ratio for energy, in dollars, per barrel of production capacity, by region and energy category.  This variable determines how many dollars of capital are required in the production of a barrel of oil equivalent in each energy category.  It therefore represents the cost of energy production.  QE is exogenous only for nuclear and renewable energy.  Values for oil, gas, and coal are computed endogenously (and depend on remaining resources) and should be examined only as indicators.  To change the cost pattern for those energy forms, use resorm and increase or decrease resources.  Values for renewable and nuclear energy can be exogenously changed, but you should maintain the initial value of the base case.  A series of gradually lower costs could represent technological progress (e.g. in the solar component of renewable).  A series of gradually higher costs could represent the impact of environmental factors (e.g. increasing costs of nuclear waste disposal).  Higher or lower values will increase or decrease investment in a particular energy category and will affect its production level.  You should be aware that investment will respond only to changes over time in QE and not to changes in the initial condition.

nodes.NAME: salpha
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sectorally-specific alpha in capital's share of value added.  This value has a general empirical base and users will not normally change it.

nodes.NAME: carsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on car sales by country/region and car type.  A value of 1.0 leaves car sales unchanged.  An increase over time to 2.0 would approximately double car sales of the specified type relative to the base case (total car sales will be normalized and therefore unchanged relative to the base case).

nodes.NAME: carstotm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on total car sales by country/region.  A value of 1.0 leaves total sales unchanged.  An increase over time to 2.0 would approximately double total sales relative to the base case (sales by type will not always change proportionately, because of differing relationships with total sales).

nodes.NAME: carsconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence time for car sales in years. This value determines the number of years over which all countries/regions will converge to the chosen function (as determined by the switch, vehfuncsw) for the computation of car sales per year.  A value of 10000 would effectively turn off convergence, so that initial country-specific variations From the function would be maintained over time.  A value of 60 would lead to near convergence by the middle of the 21st century.  Very rapid convergence seems improbable in the face of fundamental country differences in infrastructure, land area, culture, etc.

nodes.NAME: carabr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Rate of carbon absorption - this parameter defines the amoung of atmospheric carbon (expressed in billion tons) that oceans or other sinks (except forests) absorb each year. Although this value should ultimately be a function of the carbon in the atmosphere and the carbon in the sinks of the ocean, land, and biological systems (and hence a computed variable), it is common in atmospheric models to specify it as a single, constant parameter.

nodes.NAME: carinit
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial level of carbon dioxide in atmosphere in the base year, expressed in billion tons. The value in the model should be relatively accurate.

nodes.NAME: carprein
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that defines the pre-industrial atmospheric carbon levels, expressed in billion tons. Normally, a user will not change this parameter over time.

nodes.NAME: carfuel3
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Carbon generated by burning coal expressed in billion tons per billion barrels of oil equivalent.  Although this is an empirical value, it is possible that some advance technologies might sequester rather than release carbon into the atmosphere.

nodes.NAME: carfuel2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Carbon generated by burning natural gas expressed in billion tons per billion barrels of oil equivalent .  Although this is an empirical value, it is possible that some advance technologies might sequester rather than release carbon into the atmosphere.

nodes.NAME: carfuel1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Carbon generated by burning oil, expressed in billion tons per billion barrels of oil equivalent.  Although this is an empirical value, it is possible that some advance technologies might sequester rather than release carbon into the atmosphere.

nodes.NAME: carforst
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Carbon generated by deforestation - this parameter specifies the amount of atmospheric carbon (expressed in billion tons) that will be added by deforestation (expressed in billion hectares of land). Normally you would not change this parameter over time, because it should be a fairly fixed parameter.

nodes.NAME: carbtax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that sets the carbon tax, expressed in dollars/ton of carbon generated and affects (increases) energy prices and (decreases) demand. Values will normally be above 50 and as an example, a value of 100 ($100/ton) will add about $0.20 to the price of a gallon of gas.

nodes.NAME: wpsysgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, change in dispute probability with global economic growth. The value is in percent. Thus 0.1 would indicate that the probability of a dispute between two states would rise by 0.1% for each percentage point increase in global economic growth relative to the long-term average.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted From other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: hltechlinc
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the technological factor for other low income countries.

nodes.NAME: hltechssa
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the technological factor for Sub-Saharan Africa.

nodes.NAME: wpconsq
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, change in dispute threat with the square of change in power concentration (see also wpcon).  This value is used in a function as a multiplier on the square of global power concentration among great powers (PCONGREAT), a variable which itself normally ranges From approximately 0.2 to 0.4.  The change in the result of the product of the parameter and the square of concentration From year to year provides an additive term that can be interpreted as an additive increase (or decrease) in the probability of disputes between two countries/regions.

nodes.NAME: wpcon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, change in dispute threat with power concentration.  This value is used in a function as a multiplier on global power concentration among great powers (PCONGREAT), a variable which itself normally ranges From approximately 0.2 to 0.4.  The change in the result of the product From year to year provides an additive term that can be interpreted as an additive increase (or decrease) in the probability of disputes between two countries/regions.

nodes.NAME: wptrade
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, change in dispute threat with systemic trade.  The value is in percent. Thus -0.01% would indicate that the probability of a dispute between two states would fall by 0.01% for every percentage increase in world trade as a percent of global GDP.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted From other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: wpindsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A switch that can be used to turn on or off the calculations of Character of Bilateral State Interaction Score.  A value of 0 turns it off and a value greater than 0 turns it on.  1 is used to save threat, 2 is used to save Liberal Index, 3 is used to save Realist Index and 4 is used to save the COI.

nodes.NAME: hlstuntchlsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch that activates relationship between child stunting and communicable diseases. This relationship is used in the Health module to affect Communicable Diseases (Diarrhea, Respiratory Infections and Other CDs) when Child Stunting level changes From the expected value.

nodes.NAME: cdmf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Civilian damage factor.  This reactivity parameter links the severity of conventional war and the power of the opposing alliance to civilian damage (both population killed and economic capital destroyed).  A value of 0 will uncouple conventional war From damage and a value of 1 will make damage proportional to the war severity and opposing power.  There is no comparable parameter for the impact of nuclear war on civilians because the model always assumes civilian damage; in fact, it extends some such damage beyond the regions involved in nuclear war to third party countries (From fall-out and other collateral damage).

nodes.NAME: climeconimpstk
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the share of production function (technology and/or climate stock) that climate change to economic impact variable eliminates. For example, CLIMECONIMP of 2 percent times 0.5 will indicate a 1 percent reduction of stock in capital/technology.

nodes.NAME: climeconimpperctrysw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to activate climate change impact on economu using country-specific temperatures, as opposed to using global temperature. A value of 1 indicates it is on, and 0 indicates off.

nodes.NAME: climeconimplin
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameteter on linear term in the quadratic function that links changes in temperature to impact on economy in percentage terms.

nodes.NAME: climeconimpsq
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameteter on squared term in the quadratic function that links changes in temperature to impact on economy in percentage terms.

nodes.NAME: climeconimpsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to turn on the impacts of temperature rise on non-agricultural sectors.

nodes.NAME: drugusecocainem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for cocaine use.

nodes.NAME: labinformcoeffbus
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the coefficient of business index  in the multiple regression of informal labor shares.

nodes.NAME: gdpinformcoeffcorrupt
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the coefficient of Corruption Index  in the multiple regression of informal GDP shares.

nodes.NAME: labinformcoeffed
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the coefficient of education years (15+ years, both sexes)  in the multiple regression of informal labor shares.

nodes.NAME: labinformcoeffhhtrn
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the coefficient of household transfer (as a % of GDP)  in the multiple regression of informal labor shares.

nodes.NAME: infinformcoefflabinf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter can be used to change the coefficient of Informal Labor Share  in the regression of informal employment in informal enterprises.

nodes.NAME: gdpinformcoeffrand
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the coefficient of R & D spending (total, as a % of GDP)  in the multiple regression of informal GDP shares.

nodes.NAME: gdpshadowcoeffrand
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the coefficient of R & D spending (total, as a % of GDP)  in the multiple regression of shadow (informal) GDP shares.

nodes.NAME: labinformcoefftax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the coefficient of (log of) tax rate  in the multiple regression of informal labor shares.

nodes.NAME: gdpinformcoefflabinf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the coefficient of Informal Labor Share  in the multiple regression of informal GDP shares.

nodes.NAME: hlmortcdadltm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on communicable disease mortality for adults aged between 15 to 49.

nodes.NAME: hlmortcdchldm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on communicable disease mortality for children under the age of 5. This parameter exogenouslt affects mortality in the health module.

nodes.NAME: hlcomaddmort
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Communicable Disease Mortality to be added exogenously to Other Communicable Diseases.

nodes.NAME: hlcomaddprev
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Communicable Disease Prevalence to be added exogenously to Other Communicable Diseases.

nodes.NAME: hlcondomusem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the use of condoms among 15-24 year olds in high risk-sex cases. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: wpterdisp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, increase in militarized dispute probability with territorial dispute. The value is in percent. Thus 5.0 would indicate that the probability of a dispute between two states would rise by 5.0% if they have a territorial dispute outstanding, relative to the same pair without such a dispute.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted From other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: confforsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch that links the forward linkage of conflict with multifactory productivity/democracy. A value of 0 (base case) turns off the impact of intrastate conflict/state failure/fragility on multifactor productivity or democracy while a value of 1 turn it on.

nodes.NAME: sfintlwaralltoginidom
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter serves as a multiplier that adjusts the Gini coefficient based on the probability of conflict. It amplifies the Gini index by the set multiplier amount in response to the likelihood of conflict. For example, a multiplier of 1.02 typically suggests a 2% increase in the Gini coefficient. However, the actual increase is adjusted by the probability of conflict; thus, with a 50% probability of conflict, the Gini coefficient would only increase by 1%.

nodes.NAME: retireconsumrat
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Allows the user to control the spending in retirement relative to average spending at all ages.

nodes.NAME: cconstsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Consumption constant switch, with 1 indicating on and 0 indicating off.

nodes.NAME: cexovals
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Consumption exogenous values is used to set consumption values exogenously, with a value of -100 to turn the setting off.

nodes.NAME: contiguity
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The physical distance between two countries/reigons.  The scale is:  1=land contiguity; 2=0=12 miles; 3=12-24 miles; 4=24-150 miles; 5=150-400 miles; 6=more than 400 miles.  Normally you would not change this value over time.

nodes.NAME: tconr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the increase in time-related contraception use, expressed in percentage terms.

nodes.NAME: contrusm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Contraception use multiplier.  A multiplier on contraception use, by region.  It normally has a value of 1.  Higher values increase contraception use and lower values decrease it.

nodes.NAME: mfpdemoc
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Democracy contribution to MFP.

nodes.NAME: mfpconflict
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of mutlifactor productivity to domestic conflict/instability.

nodes.NAME: mfpefree
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Economic Freedom contribution to MFP.

nodes.NAME: mfpeconints
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Economic Integration by Sector to MFP.

nodes.NAME: mfpedspn
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Multifactor Productivity Growth to an increase in education spending as a share of GDP.

nodes.NAME: mfpenpri
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of multifactor productivity to energy prices.  Values (normally negative) near 0 imply little elasticity and values near -1  imply  considerable elasticity.

nodes.NAME: mfpfree
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Freedom contribution to MFP.

nodes.NAME: mfpgovcor
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Government Corruption contribution to MFP.

nodes.NAME: mfpgoveff
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Multifactor Productivity Growth to government effectiveness.

nodes.NAME: mfphlspn
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Multifactor Productivity Growth to an increase in health spending as a share of GDP.

nodes.NAME: mfpinfrindict
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of ICT contribution to MFP.

nodes.NAME: mfplife
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Multifactor Productivity Growth to an increase in life expectancy.

nodes.NAME: mfpiospn
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Multifactor Productivity Growth to changes in other infrastruction spending.

nodes.NAME: mfpedqual
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Multifactor Productivity Growth to an increase in quality scores of adult population.

nodes.NAME: mfprandd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Multifactor Productivity Growth to an increase in R&D spending as a share of GDP.

nodes.NAME: mfpedscien
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Multifactor Productivity Growth to share of tertiary graduates in science and engineering.

nodes.NAME: mfpstunt
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of multifactor productivity to stunting.

nodes.NAME: mfpinfrindtrad
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Traditional Infrastructure contribution to MFP.

nodes.NAME: mfpedvoc
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Multifactor Productivity Growth  to vocational enrollment share in secondary education.

nodes.NAME: mfpedyrs
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Multifactor Productivity Growth  to an increase in years of education for adult population.

nodes.NAME: mfphlyld
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of multifactor productivity to years of life lost to disability.

nodes.NAME: cpowdf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Conventional power damage factor.  This reactivity parameter links the severity of conventional war and the power of the opposing alliance to the losses of conventional power (personnel and equipment).  A value of 0 will uncouple conventional war From damage and a value of 1 will make damage proportional to the war severity and power of the opponents.

nodes.NAME: drcpow
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Annual depreciation rate of conventional power (coefficient).  It is in proportional terms so that 0.1 represents 10% depreciation annually.  High values could simulate arms control agreements that resulted in destruction of weapons.

nodes.NAME: cwarbase
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Conventional warfare base probability - the model adds or substracts From this value incremental probabilities of war that depend on many factors (power balances, democracy levels, etc.).  Specify values between 0 and 1 for the base annual probability of war between any actor and target.  Normally the values should be quite near 0 and in the base case all values are set to zero.

nodes.NAME: cwarf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Conventional war factor.  If WarOn = 1, by setting the value of this parameter equal to 100 or more you can force the model to generate a wide-spread war. Use of this parameter is only recommended for testing the functioning of war in the model; it has no policy interpretation.

nodes.NAME: cwarsv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Conventional war severity factor.  This coefficient determines what portion of the conventional armament potential will be used when a war erupts.  Values should range From 0 (none) to 1 (all).

nodes.NAME: mfpconv2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence of Multifactor Productivity Growth in ICT represents the time (in years) for productivity to converge to that of the service sector.

nodes.NAME: hllongvtyalphaconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence parameter that controls how fast (in how many years) the Alpha coeficient reaches its target.

nodes.NAME: extmaposnconvtimeelectran
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter represents the time required to converge to the function From the current position.

nodes.NAME: extmaposnconvtimeroadpaved
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter represents the time required to converge to the function From the current position.

nodes.NAME: extmaposnconvtimeroad
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter represents the time required to converge to the function From the current position.

nodes.NAME: ictcybevcost
nodes.Parameter Explanation: ICT cyber adverse event cost, % of GDP

nodes.NAME: landircostupper
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that sets a global upper bound value on per hectare cost of irrigation.

nodes.NAME: landircostlower
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that sets a global lower bound value on per hectare cost of irrigation.

nodes.NAME: landircostm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on cost of irrigating land by country/region.

nodes.NAME: govbuscostm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the cost of starting a business.

nodes.NAME: samadmissioncost
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the cost per SAM admission.

nodes.NAME: wpsovcount
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Count of Sovereign Countries use for estimation of the Count of Politically Relevant Dyads

nodes.NAME: envco2fert
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Effect of CO2 fertilization on crop yields.

nodes.NAME: elascd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of crop food demand to prices.  Values (normally negative) near 0 imply little responsiveness of demand to prices and larger absolute values (near -1) imply considerable responsiveness.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: ldcropm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on crop land, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase crop land and lower values decrease it.

nodes.NAME: tgrld
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Target annual growth rate in cultivated land, by region represents the desired annual growth rates for expanding cultivated land.  It is used for computation only in the initial year; thereafter the investment pattern changes endogenously in response to changing agricultural prices and costs.

nodes.NAME: cultshmp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Cultural shift on the materialism/post-materialism index.  It is an additive factor that represents the average "shift" in the index for materialism/post-materialism for a given cultural region (relative to what would be expected based of level of GDP per capita), as identified in the World Value Survey project.  The initial value is determined From data, but the user could change the value over time to represent cultural convergence or divergence.

nodes.NAME: cultshse
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Cultural shift on the survival/self-expression index.  It is an additive factor that represents the average "shift" in the index for survival/self-expression for a given cultural region (relative to what would be expected based of level of GDP per capita), as identified in the World Value Survey project.  The initial value is determined From data, but the user could change the value over time to represent cultural convergence or divergence.

nodes.NAME: cultshts
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Cultural shift on the traditional/rational-secular index.  It is an additive factor that represents the average "shift" in the index for traditional/rational-secular for a given cultural region (relative to what would be expected based of level of GDP per capita), as identified in the World Value Survey project.  The initial value is determined From data, but the user could change the value over time to represent cultural convergence or divergence.

nodes.NAME: ictconsurplusm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on ICT consumer surplus.

nodes.NAME: ICTCONSURPLUS
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Consumer-captured surpluses From cost reductions and capability enhancements as the technologies develop (i.e., surpluses not represented in standard economic measures such as gross domestic product)

nodes.NAME: ictcybbenefitm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on ICT cyber benefit.

nodes.NAME: ictcybevtcostm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on ICT cyber security risk cost.

nodes.NAME: ictcybopcostadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: ICT Cyber Security, Opportunity Cost. Addition (percent of GDP)  to change the opportunity cost compared to base case.

nodes.NAME: ictcybsecspendm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on ICT cyber security basic cost.

nodes.NAME: ICTCYBEVTCOST
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The cost of adverse cyber events stemming From hacking, cybercrime, cyber espionage, and cyber terror or war

nodes.NAME: ICTCYBOPCOST
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The potential economic benefits not realized because of forgone use of cyber-technologies in fear of adverse events or for other reasons including political control

nodes.NAME: ICTCYBBENEFIT
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The contributions to production, productivity, and therefore growth across the broader economy From investments in cyber technologies

nodes.NAME: ICTCYBRISKTOT
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The sum of adverse event costs, opportunity costs, and spending to reduce adverse events

nodes.NAME: ICTCYBRISKTOTCUM
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The sum over time of adverse event costs, opportunity costs, and spending to reduce adverse events

nodes.NAME: ictcybsecuritym
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Cyber Security Index, multiplier to change the index compared to base case exogenously

nodes.NAME: hlstddthsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for Standard Deaths. Turning it on (=1) would use standard population vector instead of country specific/dynamic population distributions.

nodes.NAME: deathtrpvm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on deaths From traffic accidents per vehicle. A value of 1 leaves values unchanged, while a value of 2 would double death per vehicle relatibe to the base case.

nodes.NAME: hivpeakdef
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the default year of HIV epidemic peak.

nodes.NAME: democimpus
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Democracy impetus coming From US or other (e.g., EU) leadership.  Values are on a 1-10 (10=most) scale, related to the Polity democracy scale.  Normally interventions with the parameter would be variable over time (e.g., increasing gradually).

nodes.NAME: democimpoth
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the democracy impetus From non-specific forces such as the spread of a systemic value around democracy. The scale ranges From 1-10 (10=most) and is based on the Polity scale.  Normally interventions with the parameter would be variable over time (e.g., increasing gradually).

nodes.NAME: democimpusn
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The neutral or normal level of democracy impetus coming From US or other (e.g., EU) leadership.  The scale ranges From 1-10 (10=most) and is based on the Polity democracy scale.   Interventions with the parameter would be very uncommon and would normally change its value for all points in time.

nodes.NAME: eldemocimp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of democracy levels with systemic leadership.  That is, the responsiveness of democracy in a country to the impetus towards democracy provided by countries/regions such as the EU or the U.S.

nodes.NAME: democwvlen
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the democracy wave length in years (peak to trough/half-wave).  Historical waves of democracy have been variable in length, so it is very reasonable to speculate that they could change From the base value or over time.

nodes.NAME: democwvmax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the maximum amplitude in Polity scale points for democracy wave.  Because the Polity democracy scale runs From 1-10 (10=most democratic), it would be highly improbable that the amplitude of any wave be more than 5-6 points.

nodes.NAME: democm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the level of democracy, expressed without units and by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, users should not generally  change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: democconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the convergence time of political variables (DEMOC) to predicted value. Very often initial data values for countries will differ From values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

nodes.NAME: dkl
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Depreciation coefficient for agricultural land investment.  This scalar (not specific to country/region) indicates the portion (e.g., 0.01 is 1%) of the investment in agricultural land (e.g. terracing or irrigation) that depreciates in a given year.  Raising it would lead to greater requirements of agricultural investment in land to maintain that land in production.

nodes.NAME: waterdesalinatedgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial growth rate of desalinated water.

nodes.NAME: waterdesalinatedm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the level of desalinated water.

nodes.NAME: desald
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Responsiveness of water price to change in prices.

nodes.NAME: desali
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Responsiveness of water price to change in stock/inventory levels.

nodes.NAME: dstlen
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Desired energy stock level as portion of stock base.  It is in proportional terms so that 0.2 represents a 20% target stock level (of a base that usually includes annual production and may include demand, exports, or imports).  There is little reason for most users to want to change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: dstl
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Desired level of stock or inventory within the economy, represented as a percentage. A value of 0.1, for instance, indicates a target stock level of 10% relative to the base case that often includes annual production and may also encompass demand, exports, or imports.

nodes.NAME: diplodistancetoeu
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The physical distance between a country and Europe (Belgium)

nodes.NAME: ginidomcnstsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Domestic Gini Index constant switch.  Values of 0 turn off and allow endogenous computation; 1 starts the consant period with the last saved value.

nodes.NAME: ginidomr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Rate of change in the domestic Gini Index. Values of 0 turn off and allow endogenous computation; non-zero values are applied to initial conditions like normal multipliers.

nodes.NAME: ginidomm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on domestic Gini Index.

nodes.NAME: hlgbdconvDown
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence time coefficient for bringing initial adjustments/normalization factors towards 1, downward convergence only

nodes.NAME: drugglobalconvsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for global convergence in drug use.

nodes.NAME: drugglobalconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence rate in global drug use.

nodes.NAME: drugusepolyindex
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Drug use index.

nodes.NAME: edprilen
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Duration of education, primary is the number of grades (years) in primary education, aggregation rule for group might result in non-integer values

nodes.NAME: wpgreat1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, increment of dispute probability in dyad with one great power.  The value is in percent probability of a dispute and is applied when at least one member of the dyad is a great power (see wpgreatthesh and wpgreatlev for definitions of great power).  That is, 0.7 would indicate that the existence of one great power would increase the probability of a dispute between two states by 0.7%, all else being equal.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted From other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: wpgreat2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, increment of dispute probability in dyad with two great powers.  The value is in percent probability of a dispute and is applied when at both members of the dyad are great powers (see wpgreatthesh and wpgreatlev for definitions of great power).  That is, 2.0 would indicate that the existence of two great powers would increase the probability of a dispute between two states by 2.0%, all else being equal.   Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted From other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).  This addition would be on top of the increment already added for the presence of one great power in a dyad (see wpgreat1).

nodes.NAME: migratebalancesw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to balance between bilateral migration (1) and monadyc migration (0)

nodes.NAME: migratesw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to replace migration in our population module using dyadic formulation

nodes.NAME: caputtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Capacity utilization target level, expressed as a ratio. For example, a target level of 0.8 signifies that the capacity utilization should reach 80% of full use. Typically, this value would remain unchanged across all years.

nodes.NAME: econfreem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on economic freedom, expressed without units and by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hdiedyrsmaxun
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the maximum education years for adults aged over 25, used for calculation of education component in HDI. Users will normally not change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: hdiedyrsminun
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the minimum education years for adults aged over 25, used for calculation of education component in HDI. Users will normally not change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: edbudgon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, parameter to turn budget impact off. Base case value is 1 (=budget impact on). Set it to 0 to bypass budget impacts entirely.

nodes.NAME: edqtqltrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A multiplier that shifts educational expenditures towards emphasis on greater quality (values below 1) or greater quantity (values above 1) .

nodes.NAME: hdiedslemaxun
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the maximum school life expectancy in education, used for calculation of education component in HDI. Users will normally not change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: hdiedsleminun
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the minimum school life expectancy in education, used for calculation of education component in HDI. Users will normally not change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: edenrsecur
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of the impact of societal insecurity  on enrollment in education.

nodes.NAME: infraelecacctrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the value of percentage access considered as universal access to electrification.

nodes.NAME: infraelecaccsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of Standard Errors to be targeted by the forecast (between -2 and 2), 0 turns off the targetting.

nodes.NAME: infraelecaccseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of years to target a given number of Standard Errors by the forecast.

nodes.NAME: infraelecaccruralcostm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter can be used to change the unit cost for a particular country or region relative to the base case.

nodes.NAME: infraelecaccurbancostm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter can be used to change the unit cost for a particular country or region relative to the base case.

nodes.NAME: infraelecacctrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access in electrification.

nodes.NAME: malelimprecisesw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for elimination of hunger; brings only the hungry population up to 1844 (no hunger) calorie level; adds to calorie needs.

nodes.NAME: malnelimstartyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the starting year towards elimination of hunger. It works in combination with malnelimtargetyr.

nodes.NAME: malnelimtargetyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the target year towards elimination of hunger. It works in combination with malnelimstarttyr.

nodes.NAME: ken
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Capital for energy, in billion dollars, by region and energy category.  This variable determines how many billion dollars of capital are required in total in each energy category.  It therefore represents the cost of energy production.

nodes.NAME: lke
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Lifetime of energy capital, years.  You will normally only change this value slowly over time, maintaining the initial value.

nodes.NAME: elasde
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy demand with price change, by region.  This value should be negative and normally will not change much over time.  Significant changes in the value From specification in the base case could lead to difficulties or instability in energy market clearing (balancing of supply and demand).

nodes.NAME: enrgdpgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Annual percentage change in energy demand as a result of technological change.  This parameter helps represent the historic phenomenon of considerable decrease over time in energy requirements per unit of economic output ("dematerialization").  It is an uncertain but very important parameter.  A value of -1 would represent an annual efficiency improvement of 1 percent.

nodes.NAME: endemm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy demand multiplier.  A multiplier on energy demand, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase demand and lower values decrease it.

nodes.NAME: enconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy demand convergence time to predicted values, in years.  Very often initial data values for countries, such as energy demand in this case, will differ a little or much From values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship or other relationship used in the model.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

nodes.NAME: elasdi
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy discoveries to prices.  This value should be positive and normally will not change much over time.  Significant changes in the value From specification in the base case could lead to difficulties or instability in energy markets.

nodes.NAME: rdinr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Rate of discovery of energy, basic annual increment.  This parameter determines the basic rate of additions to initial annual rates of fossil fuel discoveries.  That rate may not persist, however, because as resource bases near exhaustion, they gradually constrain discovery rates.

nodes.NAME: enxm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on energy exports, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase exports and lower values decrease them.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: enml
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy import limit, expressed in billion barrels of oil equivalent functions both as a switch and a numerical value, with 0 indicating no limit and positive values setting a specific limit. Positive values (above .001) limit imports to the value specified.  For instance, a specification for a country of 0 for the first five years, 2 for the next three, and 0 thereafter,  introduces a constrain on imports of two billion barrels per year during the sixth, seventh, and eighth years.  Restrictions of this kind are more often posed by exporters (see enxl) than importers.

nodes.NAME: enmm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on energy imports, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase imports and lower values decrease them.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: inputenerm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy input multiplier.  A multiplier on the use of energy as inputs in all economic sectors, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase material input and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: eninvtm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy investment by type multiplier.  A multiplier on energy investment by type, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase investment and lower values decrease it.  This parameter does not increase or decrease total energy investment; see eninvm for that.

nodes.NAME: elenpr2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy investment to change in inventory level.  Elenpr and elenpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: eleniprof2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy investment to change in profit level.  Eleniprof and eleniprof2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elenpr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy investment to inventory level.  Elenpr and elenpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: eleniprof
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy investment to profit level.  Eleniprof and eleniprof2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: eninvadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy investment additive factor.  An additive factor on energy investment, in Billion $, by region.  A value of 0 implies no change, while positive values increase investment and negative values decrease it.

nodes.NAME: eninvm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy investment multiplier.  A multiplier on energy investment, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase investment and lower values decrease it.

nodes.NAME: ennoprodsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy no production switch (1 turns off production of energy)

nodes.NAME: eprafs
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy price responsiveness to change in stock/inventory levels

nodes.NAME: epra
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy price responsiveness to stock/inventory levels.  Epra and eprafs are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities), most of which normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: enprix
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy price in dollars per barrel of oil equivalent, by region.  Energy price (ENPRI) is normally computed endogenously so as to balance supply and demand of energy.  If you set enprix to positive, nonzero values, you can override the endogenous computation with your own price level.  It is possible to intervene with energy prices only for select years by leaving enprix at zero for other years and specifying enprix only for selected ones.  You might do this, for instance, to represent a period in which government controls energy prices domestically or a cartel sets them internationally.

nodes.NAME: ENPRR(Oil)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial condition for rate of annual production growth.  Computed in the preprocessor, this initial condition heavily influences growth patterns.

nodes.NAME: ENPRR(Gas)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial condition for rate of annual production growth.  Computed in the preprocessor, this initial condition heavily influences growth patterns.

nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial condition for rate of annual production growth.  Computed in the preprocessor, this initial condition heavily influences growth patterns.

nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial condition for rate of annual production growth.  Computed in the preprocessor, this initial condition heavily influences growth patterns.

nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial condition for rate of annual production growth.  Computed in the preprocessor, this initial condition heavily influences growth patterns.

nodes.NAME: ENPRR(OthRenew)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial condition for rate of annual production growth.  Computed in the preprocessor, this initial condition heavily influences growth patterns.

nodes.NAME: eprodr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy production growth rate, expressed in decimal form (e.g., 0.035 equals 3.5 percent annual growth, by region and fuel type. This parameter can override endogenous patterns of energy production growth and force a pattern of growth for a specific fuel or set of fuels.  Growth rates are, however, constrained in the model by the availability of investment and/or resources, and may not be met.  Only positive values are allowed.  Under most circumstances, the initial value for this variable should be equal to that of enprr for the specified region and fuel type, because enprr is the empirical initial growth rate.

nodes.NAME: elenpst2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy production to change in world inventory level.  Elenpst and elenpst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elenpst
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy production to world inventory level.  Elenpst and elenpst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: enpadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy production additive factor.  An additve factor on all types of energy production, unit-less, by region.  A value of 0 implies no change, while positive values proportionately increase production and negative values decrease it.  Warning: no cost to increased production; see ENINVM and ENINVTM for parameters to shift investment and production with trade-offs.

nodes.NAME: enpm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy production multiplier.  A multiplier on all types of energy production, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase production and lower values decrease it.  Warning: no cost to increased production; see ENINVM and ENINVTM for parameters to shift investment and production with trade-offs.

nodes.NAME: squeez
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A switch that squeezes economic production when there are energy shortages (IFs does not force equilibration between energy supply and demand in any given time period, but seeks it over time; thus in the case of severe supply constraints, such as export limits by OPEC, actual shortages can appear).  A value of 0 turns off the linkage and the normal value of 1 activates it.  Other positive values also turn on the switch.  A value of 2 would make the impact of a shortage twice as great as normal and a value of 0.5 would cut it in half.

nodes.NAME: elass
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy supply with price change, by region and energy type.  There is tremendous uncertainty about these numbers.  Higher numbers will increase the responsiveness of energy supply to increased prices and lower numbers will decrease that responsiveness.  The elasticities actually work on energy investment and therefore only indirectly (and with a time delay) on energy supply.

nodes.NAME: qevremul
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier to impact the VRE cost increase as VRE share goes above threshold. A value of 1 means no impact. Values above 1 means cost increase. Values below 1 means decrease.

nodes.NAME: enon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy switch.  This switch turns on or off the linkages between the energy submodel and all others, including economics.  When off, the economic model relies upon the simpler structure of its own energy sector.  The switch enon takes values only of 1 (on) and 0 (off).  It is often useful to disconnect submodels while exploring the behavior of any one.  The normal value is 1.

nodes.NAME: edpristart
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Entrance age in primary education, aggregation rule for group might result in non-integer values

nodes.NAME: eumembsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: EU membership switch for caculations of power (0=none; 1= member).  The members of the European Union are, of course, known.  But as candidate members become full members, it would be appropriate to change the values of this parameter.

nodes.NAME: elerca1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of exchange rate to capital account/GDP ratio.  Elerca1 and elerca2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elerca2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of exchange rate to change in capital account/GDP ratio.  Elerca1 and elerca2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: edpricostadjrural
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A multiplier to adjust the marginal unit cost (per student expenditure) of primary education expanding to rural areas

nodes.NAME: edexpslconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Lower Secondary per student  expenditure as % of gdppc convergence time to function in years.  In the base case a shift From the function will be maintained because of the high convergence time.Scenarios with low convergence time make the per student cost rich those of high income countries as countries get richer. This increase in per student cost can come From lower pupil-teacher ratio, higher teacher salary and higher non-teacher salary portion of the cost.

nodes.NAME: edexperseclowrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on lower secondary per student expenditure (as % of gdppc).

nodes.NAME: edexppconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Primary per student expenditure as % of gdppc convergence time to function in years.  In the base case a shift From the function will be maintained because of the high convergence time.Scenarios with low convergence time make the per student cost rich those of high income countries as countries get richer. This increase in per student cost can come From lower pupil-teacher ratio, higher teacher salary and higher non-teacher salary portion of the cost.

nodes.NAME: edqualprispndimpgov
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A parameter to turn off/tune the impact of governance on the spending impacts on primary education quality.

nodes.NAME: edqualprispndimp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A multiplier that determines the impact of additional per student spending (as a percentage share of GDPPC) on education quality score. For example, a value of .5 would mean changing per student spending by 1 percentage point, e.g., From 10% of per capita income to 11% of the same, will add .5 to the quality score for the level of education..

nodes.NAME: edprigoalexperon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Per Primary Student expenditure (as a % of GDPPC) Goal Seek Switch. A parameter to turn goal seek on. Works with edprigoalexper

nodes.NAME: edexperprim
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on primary per student expenditure (as % of gdppc).

nodes.NAME: edprigoalexper
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Per Primary Student expenditure (as a % of GDPPC) Goal. A parameter to make the countries meet per student expenditure goals, e.g. bes practices. You must set edprigoalexperon to 1 for this to work.

nodes.NAME: edqualsecspndimpgov
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter can turn off or adjust the effect of governance on the spending impact on secondary education quality

nodes.NAME: edqualsecspndimp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A multiplier that determines the impact of additional per student spending (as a percentage share of GDPPC) on education quality score. For example, a value of .5 would mean changing per student spending by 1 percentage point, e.g., From 10% of per capita income to 11% of the same, will add .5 to the quality score for the level of education..

nodes.NAME: edexptconv
