This increase in per student cost can come From lower pupil-teacher ratio, higher teacher salary and higher non-teacher salary portion of the cost.

nodes.NAME: edexperterm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on tertiary per student expenditure (as % of gdppc).

nodes.NAME: edexpsuconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Upper Secondary per student  expenditure as % of gdppc convergence time to function in years.  In the base case a shift From the function will be maintained because of the high convergence time.Scenarios with low convergence time make the per student cost rich those of high income countries as countries get richer. This increase in per student cost can come From lower pupil-teacher ratio, higher teacher salary and higher non-teacher salary portion of the cost.

nodes.NAME: edexpersecupprm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on upper secondary per student expenditure (as % of gdppc).

nodes.NAME: hlexpcostgaptohealthel
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter  that controls link between expenditures-cost gap and health outcomes.

nodes.NAME: watresexploitrenewm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the exploitable renewable freshwater resources.

nodes.NAME: xcadjsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for export capacity adjustment. When the switch is ON, we adjust Exports based on changes in imports From main partners.

nodes.NAME: xshift
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Export shift.  An additive parameter that allows increase (positive values) or decrease (negative values) of exports of materials, manufactured goods, and services, by region.  Changes will be offset automatically by changes in private and governmental consumption.  This variable can be used to implement export-led growth strategies.  The model bases each year's exports on the proportion of its product exported the previous year, so a value of 0.05 would add 5 percent to exports for that and subsequent years.  Because the impact is cumulative, values should seldom exceed 0.1.  The initial values of trade represent data, so xshift should be changed From zero only after the initial year.

nodes.NAME: xsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on exports by sector and region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase exports and lower values decrease them.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: elxpr2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of exports to change in price.  Elxpr1 and elxpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elxpr1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of exports to price.  Elxpr1 and elxpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elasxincshock
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of exports to production and income level.  Values (normally positive) near 0  imply little change of exports with income and values near 1 imply that exports increase or decrease proportionally with income.  Normally, values should not be set far From 1.  These are used on Agriculture and Energy sectors.

nodes.NAME: elasxinc
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of exports to production and income level.  Values (normally positive) near 0  imply little change of exports with income and values near 1 imply that exports increase or decrease proportionally with income.  Normally, values should not be set far From 1.  These are used on  Materials, Manufactrues, ICT and Services sectors.

nodes.NAME: xfdifinm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on annual FDI invesment inflows. A value of 1 implies no change.

nodes.NAME: xfdistockr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Foreign Direct Investment Stock, Annual Growth Rate.

nodes.NAME: elfdilifexp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of foreign direct investment to gains in years of life expectancy.

nodes.NAME: labfemshrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on share of females in the total labor force.

nodes.NAME: hltfragepeak
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the peak age of fertility distribution.

nodes.NAME: hltfrageinit
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the initial age to start fertility distribution.

nodes.NAME: hltfrpeaklevel
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the peak level for fertility distribution

nodes.NAME: hltfrconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence parameter that controls how fast (in how many years) the Mortality Vector reaches its target

nodes.NAME: firmtaxrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government taxes imposed on firms, expressed without units and by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase taxes and lower values decrease them.

nodes.NAME: fishcatchm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on fish catch (freshwater and marine) unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase demand and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: elasfd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of food demand to prices.  Values (normally negative) near 0 imply little responsiveness of demand to prices and larger absolute values (near -1) imply considerable responsiveness.  This value normally will not change much over time.  Significant changes in the value From specification in the base case could lead to difficulties or instability in market clearing (balancing of supply and demand).

nodes.NAME: ictbroadtrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access to fixed broadband

nodes.NAME: ictbroadurimpmax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access to fixed broadband

nodes.NAME: ictbroadurimpmin
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access to fixed broadband

nodes.NAME: ictbroadsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of Standard Errors to be targeted by the forecast (between -2 and 2), 0 turns off the targetting.

nodes.NAME: ictbroadseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of years to target a given number of Standard Errors by the forecast.

nodes.NAME: aglossconsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on agricultural consumption losses adjusts the proportion of food consumption lost at the point of consumption.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: fprimt2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of food prices (meat) to changes in stock level. Fprimt1 and fprimt2 are a pair of adjustment parameters, most of which normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: fprimt1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of food prices (meat) to stock level. Fprimt1 and fprimt2 are a pair of adjustment parameters, most of which normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: fpricr2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of food prices (crops) to changes in stock level. Frpricr1 and fpricr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters, most of which normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: fpricr1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of food prices (crops) to stock level. Frpricr1 and fpricr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters, most of which normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: xfdifoutm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on annual FDI invesment outflows. A value of 1 implies no change.

nodes.NAME: forestm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on forest area, by region, expressed without units. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase forest area and lower values decrease it.

nodes.NAME: freedomm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Freedom House's measure of freedom (FREEDOM), which combines civil and political scale ranging From 2 (most free) to 14 (least free). A value of 1 in the multiplier implies no change, while higher values increase the value of FREEDOM (making a country/region less free).

nodes.NAME: govconswing
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter brings in convergence between development function determined spending and demand side (bottom-up) calculation of spending.

nodes.NAME: gdpadjsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to turn on endogenous changes on GDP over external growth rates.  If the switch is on, any scenario changes (including gdprext, mfpadd, gdsm) will affect gdpr on top of base case adjustment related to gdprest; if full control in scenarios is wanted with gdprext (new values will totally control gdpr), set switch to 0 simultaneously when making such full control changes with gdprext

nodes.NAME: histgdpforce
nodes.Parameter Explanation: GDP forcing switch, historic runs only.  A value of 1  turns on the use of historic data for GDP in an historical run.  A value of 0 turns it off.

nodes.NAME: gdprext
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Computed in the preprocessor to set economic growth rates exogenously in early model years; it should be set to 0 when using gdpadjsw to determine growth.

nodes.NAME: igdpr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial GDP growth rate, expressed in decimal form.  A value of 0.03 is equal to a rate of 3%.  Only changes in this parameter for the very first year of the model run will affect model behavior.

nodes.NAME: hdigdppcmaxun
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the maximum GDP per capita, used for calculation of  HDI component. Users will normally not change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: hdigdppcmax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: GDP per capita calculation for HDI calculation in thousands.  Users may change the parameter to represent changing global possibilities..

nodes.NAME: hdigdppcminun
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the minimum GDP per capita, used for calculation of  HDI component. Users will normally not change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: armsimmaxpctmilexp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Share of GDS(MIL) cap on MARMS

nodes.NAME: gemsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the target standard errors for GEM forecast. Value range between -2 to 2, with 0 indicating that the target is turned off. Used in combination with gemseytar.

nodes.NAME: gemm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the Gender Empowerment Measure (GEM).

nodes.NAME: gemseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies that number of years to reach the standard error target for GEM.

nodes.NAME: GINIDOM
nodes.Parameter Explanation: No longer used as a parameter (is computed as a variable).  See, instead, incshrm.

nodes.NAME: glocom
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Global community multiplier.  This global (not regional) parameter affects the probability of war  between any two geographic actors.   A value of 1 leaves the base probability unchanged.  A value of 1.5 would increase "community" by 50 percent and thereby decrease the probability of war by 50 percent.  A value of 0.5 would suggest a deterioration in global community.

nodes.NAME: xfdiwgradd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive Factor on Global Foreign Direct Investment.

nodes.NAME: globalfundsrecipients
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for global fund recipients. A value of 1 indicates on; 0 indicates off.

nodes.NAME: GINIFULL
nodes.Parameter Explanation: No longer used as a parameter (is computed as a variable).  See, instead, incshrm.

nodes.NAME: mfpbasinc
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Annual increment of growth in Multifactor Productivity Growth.

nodes.NAME: mfpbasgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Basic annual growth over time in the Multifactor Productivity Growth.

nodes.NAME: lintr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Interest rate on international loans/indebtedness, expressed in the form of a ratio. For example, setting this parameter to 0.10 represents an interest rate of 10%.

nodes.NAME: govriskm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government risk, and this affects governance security index and government quality index.

nodes.NAME: govconm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government consumption. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: govcorruptsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the target standard errors for GOVCORRUPT forecast. Value range between -2 to 2, with 0 indicating that the target is turned off. Used in combination with govcorruptseyrtar.

nodes.NAME: govcorruptseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies that number of years to reach the standard error target for GOVCORRUPT.

nodes.NAME: govcorruptm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government corruption index.

nodes.NAME: govdebtchg
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that represents an additive factor for Government debt change as % of GDP. It can represent relief by debt holders or expenditures in crisis with no net addition to recipient finances.  A value of 0 implies no net debt change by exogenous assumption.

nodes.NAME: goveffectsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the target standard errors for GOVEFFECT forecast. Value range between -2 to 2, with 0 indicating that the target is turned off. Used in combination with goveffectseyrtar.

nodes.NAME: goveffectseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies that number of years to reach the standard error target for GOVEFFECT.

nodes.NAME: goveffectm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government effectiveness index.

nodes.NAME: goveffconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the convergence time of government effectiveness to its expected value. Very often initial data values for countries will differ a little or much From values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

nodes.NAME: gdsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government expenditure by destination.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: gdscnstsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Government expenditures by destination  switch to keep constant.  A value of 1 implies switch is on, meaning GDS%GDP should be kept constant over time.

nodes.NAME: gdsedm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government expenditure on education by level.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: elgexpdebt2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of government revenues to changed in government debt levels.  Elprst1 and elprst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elgexpdebt1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of government revenues to government debt levels.  Elprst1 and elprst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: govexpm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government expenditure by destination.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: gdsnormalize
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for government finance model normalizatio. The base value of 1 normalizes all GDS to GOVCON, while a value of 0 allocates whatever is demanded by GDS and GOVCON does not get affected.

nodes.NAME: govfinconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the convergence time of government financial balances to its global function. Very often initial data values for countries will differ a little or much From values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

nodes.NAME: govbusregindm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the level of government regulation of Business Index.

nodes.NAME: govregqualsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the target standard errors for GOVREGQUAL forecast. Value range between -2 to 2, with 0 indicating that the target is turned off. Used in combination with govregqualseyrtar.

nodes.NAME: govregqualseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies that number of years to reach the standard error target for GOVREGQUAL.

nodes.NAME: govregqualm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government regulatory quality index.

nodes.NAME: HTCGRI
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Government Response to Trafficking Index

nodes.NAME: govrevtrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the target value for government revenue collection, expressed as a percentage of GDP. It is used in combination with govrevtrgtyr that defines the number of years to reach the target value From the initial year.

nodes.NAME: govrevtrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the number of years starting From the initial year by which government revenue collection reaches the target level defined by the parameter govrevtrgltlv.

nodes.NAME: elgrevdebt2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of government revenues to changes in government debt levels.  Elprst1 and elprst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: govrevm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government revenues by destination. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: elgrevdebt1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of government revenues to government debt levels.  Elprst1 and elprst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: govindsecurconflict
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Government security index term for conflict.

nodes.NAME: govindsecurgovrisk
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Government security index term for for government risk.

nodes.NAME: govindsecurviolence
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Government security index term for for violence.

nodes.NAME: govindsecurm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government security index.

nodes.NAME: gdstrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that sets the target valye of GDS target, as a share of GDP. Used in combination with gdstrgtyr.

nodes.NAME: gdsbudgetprotec
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is for budget protection. (1 = full protection, 0 is no protection) Values in between 0 and 1 indicates the share of demanded budget that will be set aside of the normalization process.

nodes.NAME: gdstrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that sets the number of years to reach the GDS target, set by gdstrgtval.

nodes.NAME: govhhpentndpctuse
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the target percentage of the required government transfers (pensions) to households, under assumptions of aging burdens.

nodes.NAME: govhhtrnwelm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government to household transfers for social welfare. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier

nodes.NAME: govhhtrnpenm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government to household transfers (pensions). A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier

nodes.NAME: hlcostgrowthel
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter controls the growth of health cost, which is managed by GDPPC growth, so if GDPPC growth if 10%, and elasticity is 0.5 then cost growth will be 5%.

nodes.NAME: mfpleadr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multifactor productivity growth rate of system leader.  This parameter is a powerful mechanism by which the user can increase or decrease the growth rate of productivity of the systemic leader (historically the U.S.).  Such changes pass through to assumptions of the rate of productivity growth in all other countries of the system.  A value of 0.01 introduces a rate of productivity growth of 1.0% annually in the systemic leader.

nodes.NAME: hltechbase
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the technological factor when not using the low income model, instead only for high income countries.

nodes.NAME: hltechshift
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the technological shift factor to alter technological change, proportional to GDP per capita.

nodes.NAME: hlmodelsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter activates linkages between health and population. Turning it on (=1) would copy Health module results for LifeExpectancy to Population module, when off leaves them in LIFEXPTMP.

nodes.NAME: cpowldcf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convention power factor representing less developed country (LDC) advantage in converting military expenditures to power ("bang for the buck").  Because of lower cost structures (as often represented by higher ratios in LDCs of GDP at purchasing power parity to  GDP at exchange rates) the same levels of military expenditures may provide greater contributions to conventional military power.  This parameter specifies the maximum relative advantage for the poorest LDCs (for instance, 2 equals twice as much power added for every dollar spent).  This parameter should probably be replaced by the typical ratio of GDP at purchasing power parity to GDP at exchange rates for a given GDP per capita.

nodes.NAME: hlmorthivmalsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for HIV and Malaria mortality. Turning it on (=1) would copy new forecast for HIV and Malaria on top of default Health module calculations, when off leaves them in HLHIVMORT and HLMALARIAMORT.

nodes.NAME: hlhivincm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on HIV incidence. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hlhivmortm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on HIV mortality. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hivculf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Cultural region-specific spread rate of HIV, expressed in percentage terms. For example, a value of 0.3 means 0.3% growth in spread rate each year.  This parameter is set for broad cultural regions such as the Islamic world and the  values have generally been set so that historic growth patterns coincide with actual tendencies in the region.

nodes.NAME: hivincr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Annual increase in the HIV infection rate during historic period, expressed in percentage terms. A value of 8 means an annual increase rate of 8% and these values are only used in the period prior to 2000.

nodes.NAME: hivmdcm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the HIV epidemic advance rates, expressed in percentage terms.

nodes.NAME: hivm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on HIV infection rate. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hivtadvr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the HIV technical advance rate to control spread of infection. This reflects simulation of social and behavioral change.

nodes.NAME: hlhivprevm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on HIV prevalence.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hivpeakyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the peak year of HIV infection. It controls the year in which the rate of infection in a population reaches its peak, before the epidemic begins to wane.

nodes.NAME: hhtaxrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government taxes imposed on households by skill level, expressed without units and by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase taxes and lower values decrease them.

nodes.NAME: ictcomputersm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Percentage of households with a Personal Computer, multiplier to change the percentage exogenously

nodes.NAME: ictintnethhm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Percentage of households with Internet access, multiplier to change the percentage exogenously

nodes.NAME: HTCTPI
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Human Trafficking Prevalence Index

nodes.NAME: inputictm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: ICT input multiplier.  A multiplier on the use of ICT as inputs in all economic sectors, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase material input and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: labempidleper
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Idle Labor percentage, is applied to reduce Labor by the given percentage.

nodes.NAME: ximfcreditr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Percentage of new Credits open each year.

nodes.NAME: ximfcrintr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Credits From IMF, outflows (Repayments).

nodes.NAME: ximfcrrepr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: IMF credit repayment rate/time (Years).

nodes.NAME: ximfcreqr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: IMF Credit to Equity Ratio.

nodes.NAME: ximfcrfinm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Credits From IMF, inflows.

nodes.NAME: marriageedseclowr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Responsiveness of lower secondary graduation rate of girls to changes in the share of girls married. A value of .5 means a increase in the graduation rate by half a percentage point for a 1 percent reduction in the share of girls who are in a marriage.

nodes.NAME: marriageedsecuppr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Responsiveness of upper secondary graduation rate of girls to changes in the share of girls married. A value of .5 means a increase in the graduation rate by half a percentage point for a 1 percent reeducation in the share of girls who are in a marriage.

nodes.NAME: mcadjsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for import capacity adjustment. When the switch is ON, we adjust Imports based on changes in exports From main partners.

nodes.NAME: mtarifftaxrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on tariff rate, by sector and region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase tariff rates and lower values decrease them. Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: msm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on import, by sector and region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase imports and lower values decrease them.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: elasmincshock
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of imports to changes in income level.  Values (normally positive) near 0  imply little change of imports with income and values near 1  imply that imports increase or decrease proportionally with income. Typically, values are not set far From 1. These are used on Agriculture and Energy

nodes.NAME: elmpr2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of imports to changes in price.  Elmpr1 and elmpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elmpr1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of imports to price.  Elmpr1 and elmpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elasminc
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of imports to income level.  Values (normally positive) near 0 imply little change of imports with income and values near 1 imply that imports increase or decrease proportionally with income. Typically, values are not set far From 1. These are used on Sectors Materials, Manufactrues, ICT and Services.

nodes.NAME: hlincoefgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: GBD Regression's Income coefficient growth.

nodes.NAME: incpovlev
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The absolute poverty level of $x per day in 2005$, so that the number of people living on less than other poverty levels (e.g. $5) can be calculated using the same variable (if it is set at other than the default value, the variable will be used to convey numbers living at the alternative level). This parameter only affects INCOMELT125LN2005.

nodes.NAME: wppowtran2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, increase in dispute probability with 10% greater power parity.  The value is in percent. Thus 0.05 would indicate that the probability of a dispute between two states would rise by 0.05% for each 10% reduction in the power differential between them (or a reduction of 0.1 on a ratio scale).  See also the threshold for the beginning of a power transition, wppowtran1.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted From other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: indirecttaxrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government taxes imposed on both households and firms for social security and welfare, expressed without units and by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase taxes and lower values decrease them.

nodes.NAME: indemm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on industrial agricultural demand, unit-less, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase demand and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: elagind
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of industrial (incl energy) use of crops with energy price.  0 turns it off.

nodes.NAME: infmormax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infant mortality maximum for PQLI calculation.  This value indicates an empirically-based value of minimum infant mortality levels (maximum in terms of quality of the value).  Users will normally not change the parameter.

nodes.NAME: infmorttfrlag
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines rate of change in moving average of infant mortality in the Total Fertility Rate equation. A value of 0 indicates no lag, 1 indicates no change and 0.9 indicates a long lag.

nodes.NAME: gdpinformshrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the informal share of GDP.

nodes.NAME: labinformshrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on share of informal labor force.

nodes.NAME: infrafinon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure Finance Model Switch.  A value of 1 (as in the base case) turns the infrastructure public financing code. 0 turns off the connection

nodes.NAME: infrainvmaintpubshrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the public share in funding maintenance of infrastructure of a specific type.

nodes.NAME: infrainvnewpubshrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the public share in funding maintenance of infrastructure of a specific type.

nodes.NAME: infrabudgetprotec
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is for budget protection by infrastructure type. (1 = full protection, 0 is no protection) Values in between 0 and 1 indicates the share of demanded budget that will be set aside From the budget allocated for infrastructure in the government finance model.

nodes.NAME: DIPLOINGOADVOCACY
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The number of advocacy INGOs operating in, on or about a country.

nodes.NAME: DIPLOINGOPROGRAM
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The number of programmatic INGOs operating in, on or about a country.

nodes.NAME: enprixi
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy base equilibium price in dollars per barrel of oil equivalent, by region.  Energy price (ENPRI) is normally computed relative to a price given in the initial or base year.  If that price is consdered far From long-term equilibirum, this parameter can overide it endogenously.  If you set enprixi to positive, nonzero values, you can override the initial oil price with your own price level.

nodes.NAME: gdpinformcoeffintercept
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the intercept of the multiple regression of informal GDP shares.

nodes.NAME: infinformcoeffintercept
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter can be used to change the intercept of the regression of informal employment in informal enterprises.

nodes.NAME: gdpshadowcoeffintercept
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the intercept of the multiple regression of shadow (informal) GDP shares.

nodes.NAME: xportr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Basic Growth Rate on International Portfolio Investment, Inward Stocks.

nodes.NAME: GINI
nodes.Parameter Explanation: No longer used as a parameter (is computed as a variable).  See, instead, incshrm.

nodes.NAME: idsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on investment, by sector and region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase investment and lower values decrease it. Investment across sectors are normalized. Thus changes in one sector will affect others. Patameter invm should be used to change total investment. Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: invm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on all types of investment, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase investment and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: migrater
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Net migration of a population in percent per year (negative values reflect emigration and positive values reflect immigration).  Because global emigration and immigration must balance, changes in this value for a single country/region may not change migration/population as substantially as the change introduced in migrater.

nodes.NAME: migrateinm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Inward migration of a population in percent per year.  Because global emigration and immigration must balance, changes in this value for a single country/region may not change migration/population as substantially as the change introduced originally.

nodes.NAME: xportfoliom
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on International Portfolio Investment, Inward Stocks.

nodes.NAME: xfdistockm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Foreign Direct Investment Stocks of Investments From Abroad.

nodes.NAME: landirareaactualm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on land area actually irrigated.

nodes.NAME: landirlife
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that sets the lifetime value of irrigation infrastructure.

nodes.NAME: labmarketsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to turn on the impact of changes in labor demand to computation of value added (normally supply affects it and changes more slowly)

nodes.NAME: labdemsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on labor demand, by country/region, sector and skill.

nodes.NAME: labretagem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on labor force retirement age. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year

nodes.NAME: LAPOPR
nodes.Parameter Explanation: No longer used as parameter.  Now a computed variable.

nodes.NAME: labparm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on labor participation rate. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value.

nodes.NAME: labunemprtrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Number of years (From the base year) to get to the long term unemployment rate target for labor market equilibration, used in conjunction with labunemprtrgtval.

nodes.NAME: labwagesexratm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the ratio of female to male wages.  Base case value of the parameter is 1. Values above 1 will increase the ratio, i.e., female wage will go up more than the male wage. Values less than 1 will decrease female wage relative to the male.

nodes.NAME: landarablepotmed
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Potentially arable land represents the maximum crop land value for each country based on the medium value From Eitelberg et al. 2015

nodes.NAME: landarablepotlow
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Potentially arable land represents the maximum crop land value for each country based on the low value From Eitelberg et al. 2015

nodes.NAME: landarablepot
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Potentially arable land represents the maximum crop land value for each country.

nodes.NAME: landarablepotsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for arable land. A value of 3 indicates high potential, 2 indicates medium, and 1 indicates low potential for arable land.

nodes.NAME: LD(Crop)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Land in million hectares, by region and land category.  You can change this initial condition to represent different assumptions about land availability for agriculture.  Only initial values can be changed; the model subsequently computes land by category endogenously.

nodes.NAME: LD(Grazing)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Land in million hectares, by region and land category.  You can change this initial condition to represent different assumptions about land availability for agriculture.  Only initial values can be changed; the model subsequently computes land by category endogenously.

nodes.NAME: LD(Forest)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Land in million hectares, by region and land category.  You can change this initial condition to represent different assumptions about land availability for agriculture.  Only initial values can be changed; the model subsequently computes land by category endogenously.

nodes.NAME: LD(Other)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Land in million hectares, by region and land category.  You can change this initial condition to represent different assumptions about land availability for agriculture.  Only initial values can be changed; the model subsequently computes land by category endogenously.

nodes.NAME: LD(Urban)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Land in million hectares, by region and land category.  You can change this initial condition to represent different assumptions about land availability for agriculture.  Only initial values can be changed; the model subsequently computes land by category endogenously.

nodes.NAME: landirareaequipm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on land area equipped for irrigation.

nodes.NAME: landirareasat
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Maximul land area that can be irrigated. If it does not exceed the land irrigated for a country/region, expansion is not possible via scenario.

nodes.NAME: hdilifemaxf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Life expectancy minimum for HDI calculation, in years.  Users may change the parameter to represent growing life expectancy.

nodes.NAME: hdilifemax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Life expectancy minimum for PQLI calculation, in years.  Users will normally not change the parameter.

nodes.NAME: hdilifemaxun
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the maximum life expectancy, used for calculation of  HDI component. Users will normally not change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: hdilifeminun
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the minimum life expectancy, used for calculation of  HDI component. Users will normally not change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: lifexpmin
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the minimum life expectancy for PQLI calculation, expressed in years. Users will normally not change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: HLCOSTLE
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The cost of applying the life extension treatment to the entire adult population (at or older than 30)

nodes.NAME: HLCOSTLESUB
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The subsidy that low income countries received for getting the life extension treatment, based on GDPPC relationship with the US in the base year

nodes.NAME: hlcostleyrper
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Cost of the Life Extension intervension for the SENS project in Thousand $ per year person

nodes.NAME: hlcostletime
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Duration of the Life Extension intervension for the SENS project in years, meaning that people need to take the treatment again after this amount of years

nodes.NAME: lks
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Lifetime of capital by sector, expressed in years.  You will normally only change this value slowly over time, maintaining the initial value.

nodes.NAME: nwarf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Nuclear war factor.  This is a reactivity parameter that relates the severity of a conventional war to the probability that nuclear war will erupt between acting and reacting alliances.  A value of 0 eliminates the possibility of nuclear war; a value of 1 creates a probability of war equal to the severity of conventional war (see cwarf).  By setting the value equal to 100 or more you can force the model to generate a war whenever a conventional war erupts.

nodes.NAME: feddemm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on all livestock feed demand, by region and without units. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase demand and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: elglinpr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of livestock grazing intensity to prices.  Values (normally positive) near 0 would imply little change of grazing with livestock prices and values near 1 would imply that grazing increases or decreases proportionally with prices.

nodes.NAME: livhdpro
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Represents the productivity gains in livestock herds due to grain feeding, functioning as a multiplier-index. Normally, users should adjust this value gradually, starting with the initial value.

nodes.NAME: lvherdm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on livestock herd.

nodes.NAME: slr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Livestock slaughter rate coefficient represents the proportion of herd slaughtered annually. For example, a rate of 0.7 means 70% of the herd is slaughtered each year.

nodes.NAME: lvcf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Livestock to calorie conversion factor, compared to crops.

nodes.NAME: edseclowrlen
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Duration of education, lower secondary is the number of grades (years) in lower secondary education, aggregation rule for group might result in non-integer values

nodes.NAME: edseclowrenrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier applied directly on lower secondary enrollment rate. Values greater (less) than 1 results in growth (decline) From the base level forecast when the multiplier value is 1. (Note: Transition and graduation rate parameters can also be used to bring in enrollment change. This parameter affects all but the first grade)

nodes.NAME: edseclowrdrpgrdm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier applied directly on a specific grade dropout rate in lower secondary. Values greater (less) than 1 results in growth (decline) From the base level forecast when the multiplier value is 1.

nodes.NAME: edseclowrenrgrdm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier applied directly on a specific grade enrollment rate in lower secondary. Values greater (less) than 1 results in growth (decline) From the base level forecast when the multiplier value is 1.

nodes.NAME: edseclowrgradgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, lower secondary (general), Graduation rate to the last grade, annual additive growth. A parameter to make the countries meet education targets by an annual additive growth in the survival rate in general lower secondary.

nodes.NAME: edseclowrgndreqgrad
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education lower sec, no of years by which gender parity index for graduation rate reaches 1. The gender parity index is the ratio of the male rate to the female rate. Must set edgndreqsuron=1 for this to work.

nodes.NAME: edseclowrgratrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve 100% Graduation rate From primary to lower secondary education.

nodes.NAME: edseclowrgram
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Lower Secondary Graduation Rate Multiplier.

nodes.NAME: edseclowrtrangr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, lower secondary (general), transion rate From primary, annual additive growth. A parameter to make the countries meet education targets by an annual additive growth in the rate of transition From primary to general lower secondary.

nodes.NAME: edseclowrgndreqtran
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education lower sec, no of years by which gender parity index for transition rate raeches 1. The gender parity index is the ratio of the male rate to the female rate.

nodes.NAME: edseclowrtrantrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal transition rate From primary to lower secondary education.

nodes.NAME: edseclowrtranm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Lower Secondary Transition Rate Multiplier.

nodes.NAME: edseclowrvocadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Lower Secondary, additive factor to change share of total vocational enrollment (ex.: value of .1 takes share From 30% to 40%)

nodes.NAME: edterpushon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, parameter to slow down the impacts on tertiary enrollment From an education push at the lower levels of education

nodes.NAME: hlmalariaincm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on malaria incidence.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hlmalariamortm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on malaria mortality.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hlmalariaprevm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on malaria prevalence.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: malemigr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Male migration as a portion of total migration.  This parameter is expressed as a ratio value, so that .47 would mean 47%.

nodes.NAME: birthmshr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Births, male share.  Slightly more than 50% of births are males and more males die at most ages than do females.  This is an empirical value and you would normally not want to change it.

nodes.NAME: malnpoppsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for malnourished population. A value of 1 indicates that the effect is on and uses full distribution, while a value of 0 indicates off (as in the base case).

nodes.NAME: malnhldsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to hold the forecast of malnutrition among children.

nodes.NAME: hlmlnsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter activates linkages between malnutrition and communicable diseases. It is used in the health module to affect communicable diseases when malnutrition changes From expected values. A value of 1 indicates on; 0 indicates off.

nodes.NAME: malnm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multplier on malnutrition among the population. A value of 1 represents no change, 1.25 represents a 25 percent increase and .75 represents a 25 percent decrease.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: malnconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the convergence time of political variables to its expected value.  Very often initial data values for countries will differ a little or much From values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

nodes.NAME: womeninleadershipm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on managerial roles filled by women. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: inputmanum
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Manufacture input multiplier.  A multiplier on the use of manufactured good as inputs in all economic sectors, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase material input and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: inputmatem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Material input multiplier.  A multiplier on the use of materials as inputs in all economic sectors, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase material input and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: matpostradd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor to introduce a shift in Materialism/post-materialism index for a region/country.  It increases or decreases the index value that the model calculates.  The normal value is zero.  See also and contrast with cultshmp, which is a cultural shift for the large cultural regions identified in the WVS project and which is calculated From data.

nodes.NAME: mprconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the convergence time of Materialism/postmaterialism to expected valye based on the analytic function. Very often initial data values for countries will differ a little or much From values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

nodes.Parameter Explanation: Maximum meat consumption per person, expressed in tons per person per year   limits meat consumption calculations for the initial year, in case of unreasonable data. nodes.NAME: elasmd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of meat demand to prices.  Values (normally negative) near 0 imply little responsiveness of demand to prices and larger absolute values (near -1) imply considerable responsiveness.  This value normally will not change much over time.  Significant changes in the value From specification in the base case could lead to difficulties or instability in market clearing (balancing of supply and demand).

nodes.NAME: migrateinr

nodes.NAME: migrateinadd

nodes.NAME: migrateoutr

nodes.NAME: migrateoutadd

nodes.NAME: enxl
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy export limit, ex billion barrels of oil equivalent  functions both as a switch and a numerical value, with 0 indicating no limit and positive values setting a specific limit..  Positive values (above .001) limit exports to the value specified.  For instance, a specification for a country of 0 for the first five years, 2 for the next three, and 0 thereafter,  introduces a constrain on exports of two billion barrels per year during the sixth, seventh, and eighth years.  If placed on OPEC exports, such an export restriction would be very severe.

nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for mortality modification. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase mortality and lower values decrease it.  Users would introduce an epidemic (like AIDS) by substantially increasing the value.  Scientific advance that greatly increased our age spans could be introduced by a value of 0.5 that is normally phased in.

nodes.NAME: hlscaleconvdown
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the convergence years for mortality being higher than distal driver forecasts. This switch is normally set to off (0).  When turned on it sets the number of years over which an intial  scaling factor computed the first year (the ratio of mortality to distal driver-based expectations) is converged to 1.0.

nodes.NAME: mfpadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor on Multifactor Productivity Growth.  This parameter is a powerful mechanism by which the user can increase or decrease the growth rate of countries around assumptions of the rate of productivity growth.  Normally values would be 0.0.  A value of 0.01 would introduce an added productivity growth of 1.0% annually.

nodes.NAME: igdprcor
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial GDP corrected growth rate, expressed in decimal form.  A value of 0.03 is equal to a rate of 3%.  Only changes in this parameter for the very first year of the model run will affect model behavior.

nodes.NAME: nsnaratm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Mutliplier on the ratio of the mean consumption in survey and national accounts approaches to their calculation.  The ratio is calculated the first year, and changes in the multiplier From 1 allow the user to posit increases or deceases.This parameter only affects the old INCOMELT125LN2005 and INCOMELT200LN2005.

nodes.NAME: workageretirendpctuse
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Percent of needed retirement age needed to deal with aging set to be used.

nodes.NAME: swingstsdem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Swing state democracy effects From global, swing state, and regional democracy levels.  These parameters have been estimated and you will seldom change them. Values of 0 turn off the respective effects.

nodes.NAME: neonatmorm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Neonatal mortality rate multiplier. Multiplier on NEONATMORM, unitless, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase NEONATMORM (up to 90% of INFMORM) and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial.

nodes.NAME: carannwi
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter sets the initial net emissions From fossil fuels.

nodes.NAME: nsdiv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: North-South dividing line, GDP per capita.  This parameter is only used in computing summary measures of the north-south gap in absolute or relative terms.

nodes.NAME: elndpow
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of nuclear damage with nuclear power.  Values (normally positive) near 0 would imply little elasticity and values near 1 would imply very considerable elasticity.  Changes in this parameter will only have an effect when the model generates a nuclear war.

nodes.NAME: nmilf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Nuclear military expenditure factor.  A coefficient determining what portion of a country's or region's military expenditure is devoted to nuclear weapons, including delivery systems.  For instance, 0.1 would result in 10 percent.  This can be changed over time and could be used to convert a traditionally nuclear-free region into a nuclear power.  Normal values will range From 0 to 0.2.

nodes.NAME: drnpow
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Annual depreciation rate of nuclear power (coefficient).  It is in proportional terms so that 0.1 represents 10% depreciation annually.  High values could simulate arms control agreements that resulted in destruction of weapons.

nodes.NAME: npowf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Nuclear power factor, warheads/billion $ expenditure.

nodes.NAME: nwarsv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Nuclear war severity factor.  This coefficient determines what portion of the nuclear armament potential will be used when a war erupts.  Values should range From 0 (none) to 1 (all).

nodes.NAME: govnucwpadd

nodes.NAME: diploingoadvocacyconv

nodes.NAME: druguseopiatesm

nodes.NAME: hlcostotherrattarget

nodes.NAME: HLCOSTOTHER

nodes.NAME: migrateoutm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Migration rate multiplier outward.  A multiplier on migration rate , unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase mortality and lower values decrease it.

nodes.NAME: xportstoutm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Portfolio Investment, outward stocks.

nodes.NAME: xfdistoutm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Foreign Direct Investment (Outflows).

nodes.NAME: hivpeakr

nodes.NAME: ictindexm

nodes.NAME: prdthreshold
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Used to adjust the value of the threshold used for determining political relevance for THREAT.

nodes.NAME: democpolitysetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter sets the target standard errors to be forecasted for DEMOC. Values range between -2 to 2, with 0 indicating that the target standard errors are turned off. This parameter is used in combination with democpolityseyrtar.

nodes.NAME: democpolyarchyadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor to the Polyarchy Index.

nodes.NAME: democpolyarchym

nodes.NAME: hlhivartm

Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: xportwgrm

nodes.NAME: wpthrwar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, portion of all disputes that escalate to wars.  The value is in percent. Thus 3.3 would indicate that the probability of a war between two states would be 3.3% if they experienced a militarized international dispute (or 0.33% if the probability of a dispute were 10%).  This parameter is not now being use to generate wars From disputes.

nodes.NAME: povagesexgeneric
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for initialization of the poverty profile. A value of 0 (as in the base case) will use country specific age-sex poverty rates for model initialization. A value of 1 will use age-sex poverty rates From a generic profile for initializing all countries.

nodes.NAME: povagesexdynamic
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for poverty profile forecast. A value of 0 (as in the early version base case) will freeze age-sex poverty rates for the model horizon. A value of 1 will use dynamic models (full model base case) for  age-sex poverty rates.

nodes.NAME: povagesexnormstatic
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for normalization of the poverty profile. A value of 0 (as in the base case) will normalize age-sex poverty rates with the national poverty rate forecast. A value of 1 will normalize  age-sex poverty rates using a constant national poverty rate, for example, the base year rate.

nodes.NAME: povagesexagratnat
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch that determines the ratio of age-group poverty to national poverty. A value of 0 merges the ratio to a target level, i.e., the average of high income countries while any other value sets it to the multiple of initial.

nodes.NAME: wpconmax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, maximum power concentration affecting dispute probability.  This parameter bounds the power concentration range within which change affects dispute probability.

nodes.NAME: wpconmin
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, minimum power concentration affecting dispute probability.  This parameter bounds the power concentration range within which change affects dispute probability.

nodes.NAME: wppowtran1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, ratio of power where transition begins.  If the value were 0.7 it would indicate that when the weaker power in a dyad reached 0.7 (or 70%) of the power of the stronger, a power transition would begin.

nodes.NAME: co2prein
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that defines the pre-industrial level of atmospheric CO2 in parts per million. Normally, a user would not change this parameter over time. See also carprein - that sets the pre-industrial atmospheric carbon levels in billion tons.

nodes.NAME: encartpp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy cartel price premium.  This is a parameter (normally 0) that indicates the number of dollars/barrel that an energy cartel could add to global energy prices.  Normally a scenario using this parameter would introduced it for a specific period (e.g., 2020-2025) to represent a tight energy market allowing such a cartel to be effective, at least for a time.

nodes.NAME: elprst2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of prices to change in stock/inventory levels.  Elprst1 and elprst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elprst1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of prices to stock/inventory levels.  Elprst1 and elprst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: edqualpriallm
