Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: edprienrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier applied directly on primary enrollment rate. Values greater (less) than 1 results in growth (decline) From the base level forecast when the multiplier value is 1. (Note: Intake and survival rate parameters can also be used to bring in enrollment changes. This parameter affects all but the first grade)

nodes.NAME: edpridrpgrdm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier applied directly on a specific grade dropout rate in primary. Values greater (less) than 1 results in growth (decline) From the base level forecast when the multiplier value is 1.

nodes.NAME: edprienrgrdm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier applied directly on a specific grade enrollment rate in primary. Values greater (less) than 1 results in growth (decline) From the base level forecast when the multiplier value is 1.

nodes.NAME: edprigndreqintn
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education primary, no of years (From firstyear) by which gender parity in net primary intake rate is reached. The gender parity index is the ratio of the male rate to the female rate. Must set edgndreqintnon=1 for this to work.

nodes.NAME: edqualprimathm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education quality, primary, math score multiplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: edpriintngr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Primary Net Intake Rate Anuual Growth Rate. A parameter to make the countries meet education targets by an annual percentage growth in net intake rate.

nodes.NAME: edpriintntrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal net intake rate in primary education.

nodes.NAME: edpriintnm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Primary Net Intake Rate Multiplier.

nodes.NAME: edqualprireadm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education quality, primary, reading score multiplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: edqualpriscim
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education quality, primary, science score multiplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: edprisurgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Primary Survival Rate Annual Growth Rate. A parameter to make the countries meet education targets by an annual percentage growth in survival rate.

nodes.NAME: edprigndreqsur
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education primary, no of years (From firstyear) by which gender parity in primary survival rate is reached. The gender parity index is the ratio of the male rate to the female rate. Must set edgndreqsuron=1 for this to work.

nodes.NAME: edprisurtrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve 100% Survival Rate in primary education.

nodes.NAME: edprisurm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Primary Survival Rate Multiplier.

nodes.NAME: HLEXPENDPRIV
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The total Health Expenditure includes 2 components, Public (GDS - Health) and private HLEXPENDPRIV

nodes.NAME: ictcybevprob
nodes.Parameter Explanation: ICT cyber adverse event probability, 0-1

nodes.NAME: prodtf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Production of energy, minimum reserve ratio.  This value specifies the minimum number of years of reserves, at current rates of production, that can exist for any fossil energy fuel.  Thus a value of 10 would mean that when reserves dropped below 10 years of production, production would be cut to restore the minimum ratio.

nodes.NAME: tefinfadjm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the adjustment of productivity (TEF) because of the extent of informal economy. A value of 0 indicates no adjustment and a value of 1 indicates full adjustment.

nodes.NAME: tfpshockadjshr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: In economic shock such as COVID period, the proportion of change to GDP that has persistent impact on TFP (TEFF); rest of affect goes to temporary capacity utilization.

nodes.NAME: protecm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on trade protection, by region allows user to adjust the price of imported goods, relative to the base case. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the prices of imported goods and lower values decrease them.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: randdexpm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on R&D expenditure.   A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hwf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Historical (inertial delay) weight in change of expected economic growth.  Values near 1.0 imply very rapid adjustment and values near 0 imply little or no adjustment.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: rdm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy reserve discovery multiplier, unit-less.  This parameter normally has a value of 1.  A value of 1.5 would increase annual fossil fuel discoveries by 50 percent (within the limit of ultimate resources, but without additional investment in energy discovery), while a value of 0.5 would decrease it by 50 percent.

nodes.NAME: rdi
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Rate of discovery for fossil fuels, initial, billion barrels of oil equivalent.  Changes in this parameter only directly effect rates of discovery in the very first year; thereafter the rates are calculated.

nodes.NAME: hlcostotherrattargetconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the number of years  to reach the target for the ratio of cost other to (Mortality + Morbidity + Life Extension) cost.

nodes.NAME: xfdioutf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Home Country Reduction in Investment for every unit of FDI outflow.

nodes.NAME: wpally
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, reduction of dispute threat with alliance in dyad.  The value is in percent probability of a dispute.  That is, -0.1 would indicate that being in an alliance would reduce the probability of a dispute between two states by 0.1%, all else being equal.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted From other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: samrrsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to turn on/off the relative risk effect of SAM.

nodes.NAME: hlproxdrvrrsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Relative risk switch for proximate drivers in health module. Setting the switch to any value above 0 will copy the content of the respective table, detailed in HealthProxDrivRRsList, to the RR table used in the run of the model. Leaving the parameter off (=0) will restore the base case.

nodes.NAME: qevrethr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A parameter to set the percentage share of VRE in total energy use at which VRE costs (QE) starts to increase.

nodes.NAME: waterrenewconverge
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the time for country to return to exploitable limit of renewable freshwater resources.

nodes.NAME: repayrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on loan repayment allows user to increase or decrease the target debt level.  A value of 0 means that all debt should be repayed (equilibrium dynamics will work around 0); values above 1 increase tolerance for debt.

nodes.NAME: hlpm2pt5sw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the effect on respiratory diseases and infections when residential PM2.5 level changes From the expected values.

nodes.NAME: envpm25hldsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to hold the forecast of residential PM2.5 air pollution levels. A value of 0 indicates off; 1 indicates on.

nodes.NAME: envpm2pt5m
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the level of residential 2.5 air pollution.

nodes.NAME: resor
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Resources of fossil fuels, ultimate, billion barrels of oil equivalent.  This value only sets an initial condition; thereafter resources are computed taking into account depletion From production.

nodes.NAME: resorm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Ultimately recoverable resource multiplier, by energy type.  This parameter allows the user to increase or decrease ultimately recoverable resource values.  A value of 1 accepts the values of RESOR as specified.  A value of 1.5 would raise the resource levels for a specific energy form in a specific country/region by 50 percent.  This multiplier is unusual in that it is only important in the first year - it should not be changed over time because after ultimate resources are calculated the first year they can only run down (be used up).

nodes.NAME: resoruncon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Resources of unconventional fossil fuels, ultimate, billion barrels of oil equivalent.  This value only sets an initial condition; thereafter resources are computed taking into account depletion From production.

nodes.NAME: resorunconm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Ultimately recoverable unconventional resource multiplier, by energy type.  This parameter allows the user to increase or decrease ultimately recoverable resource values.  A value of 1 accepts the values of RESOR as specified.  A value of 1.5 would raise the resource levels for a specific energy form in a specific country/region by 50 percent.  This multiplier is unusual in that it is only important in the first year - it should not be changed over time because after ultimate resources are calculated the first year they can only run down (be used up).

nodes.NAME: wpcontiguity
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, response of dispute threat to geographic contiguity/proximity.  The value is in percent probability of a dispute.  That is, 3.0 would indicate that being neighbors would increase the probability of a dispute between two states by 3.0%, all else being equal.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted From other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: wpcommun
nodes.Parameter Explanation: War probability elasticity with global community.  This parameter and the underlying level of global community (GLOCOM) are not now being used in the calculation of threat.

nodes.NAME: wpdemdist
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, response of dispute threat to political distance.  The value is in percent probability of a dispute and is applied to the absolute value of the distance in democracy level between the states in a dyad.  That is, 0.01 would indicate that every point of additional distance on the underlying Polity scale would increase the probability of a dispute between two states by 0.01%, all else being equal.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted From other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: wpdemmin
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, response of dispute threat to minimum democracy level in dyad.  The value is in percent probability of a dispute and is applied to the democracy level in the less democratic state in a dyad.  That is, -0.01 would indicate that every point of additional democracy on the underlying Polity scale would reduce the probability of a dispute between two states by 0.01%, all else being equal.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted From other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: GOVRISK
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The Risk Index is a weigthed average of the contribution to risk of a set of aproximately 20 variables. Each variable can contribute From 0 to 1 depending on where its value sits in the Minimum to Maximum range.

nodes.NAME: infraroadunpavedcostm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for changing the cost of construction for a kilopmeter of unpaved road.

nodes.NAME: infraroadraisetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of Standard Errors to be targeted by the forecast (between -2 and 2), 0 turns off the targetting.

nodes.NAME: infraroadraitrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the value of percentage access considered as universal access to all weather roads within two kilometers for people in the rural areas.

nodes.NAME: infraroadraiseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of years to target a given number of Standard Errors by the forecast.

nodes.NAME: infraroadraitrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access to roads.

nodes.NAME: sanithhlifepitlatrinetrad
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, sanitation, rural traditional pit latrine, lifetime in years

nodes.NAME: watsafetrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the value of percentage with no access considered as universal access to safe water (for example, 0 percent)

nodes.NAME: watsafhldsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to hold the forecast of Safe Water at Base year levels

nodes.NAME: watsafenoconsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of Standard Errors to be targeted by the forecast (between -2 and 2), 0 turns off the targetting.

nodes.NAME: watsafenoconseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of years to target a given number of Standard Errors by the forecast.

nodes.NAME: watsafem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for the percentage of People living with different levels of Access to Safe Water

nodes.NAME: samtomalnchpsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to activate linkage between SAM and Malnutrition. A value of 1 indicates on, setting averted SAM cases to malnourished (instead of fully healthy).

nodes.NAME: samadmissionadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor for percentage of SAM cases admitted for treatment.

nodes.NAME: samadmissionm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on percentage of SAM cases admitted for treatment. A value of 1 represents no change, 1.25 represents a 25 percent increase and .75 represents a 25 percent decrease.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: samadmissionsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for percentage of SAM cases admitted for treatment. A value of 0 shows regular forecast, 1 keeps zeroes constant and a value of 2 keep all constant.

nodes.NAME: samavertedm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Mutliplier on the percentage of SAM cases successfully treated. A value of 1 represents no change, 1.25 represents a 25 percent increase and .75 represents a 25 percent decrease.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: samavertedconvyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence time for averted SAM cases.

nodes.NAME: malnchpsamtostunt
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of SAM on stunting. This parameter is used to increase or decrease the effect of severe acute malnutrition on stunting.

nodes.NAME: sanitationtrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the  value of percentage with household connections considered as universal access to sanitation.

nodes.NAME: sanitbudgetprotec
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is for budget protection of sanitation services spending. Values greater than 1 raises the cost relative to the base case value for the same year. Values lower than 1 lowers the cost.

nodes.NAME: sanithldsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to hold the forecast of Sanitation at Base year levels

nodes.NAME: sanitationimpcostm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter to change the unit cost relative to the base case.

nodes.NAME: sanithhmodel2sw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sanitation Model Switch, Value of 1 Switches to the Regression Model with No Poverty

nodes.NAME: sanitnoconsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of Standard Errors to be targeted by the forecast (between -2 and 2), 0 turns off the targetting.

nodes.NAME: sanitnoconseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of years to target a given number of Standard Errors by the forecast.

nodes.NAME: sanithhm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for the percentage of people living with different levels of access to sanitation services. Values greater than 1 raises access relative to the base case value for the same year. Values lower than 1 reduce access.

nodes.NAME: sanithhbasictrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sanitation services, at least basic, target value to be reached by a certain number (sanithhbasictrgtyr) of years starting From the model base year. Default value is 100.

nodes.NAME: sanithhbasictrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sanitation services, at least basic, years From model base year to reach the target value stored in the parameter sanithhbasictrgtval. The year count starts From the initial year of the mdoel.

nodes.NAME: sanithhsafetrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sanitation Services, Safely Managed, years From model base year to reach the target value stored in the parameter sanithhsafetrgtval. The year count starts From the initial year of the mdoel.

nodes.NAME: sanithhsafetrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sanitation Services, Safely Managed,  target value to be reached by a certain number (sanithhsafetrgtyr) of years starting From the model base year. Default value is 100

nodes.NAME: sanithhcostlowershr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, Sanitation services, share of services using lower-cost service. Base case value is 50/50 when both lower and upper cost services are available

nodes.NAME: sanitationexovals
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sanitation Exogenous Values (-100 is off)

nodes.NAME: sanitationm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for the percentage of People living with different levels of Access to Sanitation

nodes.NAME: savingsdiscountrt
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Discount rate used to compute working age  and savings rate needed with changes in Life Expectancy.

nodes.NAME: cpctnduse
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Proportion of required consumption that is allocated to address the impact of aging.

nodes.NAME: edqualsecmathm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education quality, secondary, math score multiplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: edqualsecallm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education quality, secondary, multiplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: edqualsecreadm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education quality, secondary, reading score multiplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: edqualsecscim
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education quality, secondary, science score multiplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: elinst2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of sectoral investment to changes in stock level.  Elinst1 and elinst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elinst1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of sectoral investment to stock level.  Elinst1 and elinst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: sanithhlifesst
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, sanitation, septic, sewerage, treatment facilities, lifetime in years

nodes.NAME: inputservm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Service input multiplier.  A multiplier on the use of service as inputs in all economic sectors, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase material input and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: malnchpsamadj
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Adjustment parameter for incidence of Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM).  A value of 1 represents Incidence is equal to prevalence. Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: malnchpsamm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM).  A value of 1 represents no change, 1.25 represents a 25 percent increase and .75 represents a 25 percent decrease.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: gdpshadowcoeffcorrupt
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the coefficient of Corruption Index  in the multiple regression of shadow (informal) GDP shares.

nodes.NAME: gdpshadowcoefflabinf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the coefficient of Informal Labor Share in the multiple regression of shadow (informal) GDP shares.

nodes.NAME: gdpshadowshrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the shadow (informal) GDP share.

nodes.NAME: gdpshadowon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for Shadow/Informal economy. A value of  1 turns on  the shadow economy, 0 turns on the informal economy (as in the base case)

nodes.NAME: marriedfemshrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for the share of female who are in a marriage or a union. Values greater than 1 raises the share relative to the base case value for the same year. Values lower than 1 lowers the share.

nodes.NAME: hlsmimpsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This switch is used to turn off the estimation of Smoking Impact, thus keeping the values constant after 2030. The GBD original forecast goes only until 2030.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingdecm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on exponential/logarithmic rate of decrease in smoking among adults aged above 30.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingincm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on exponential rate of increase in smoking among adults aged above 30.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingceiling
nodes.Parameter Explanation: User can specify maximum smoking prevalence, Impacts countries rising through stage 2 (risking to peak).

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingfloor
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Minimum smoking prevalence among adults aged over 30.

nodes.NAME: hlsmkimeff
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter controls the shorter term impact of smoking rate on smoking.

nodes.NAME: hlsmkel
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter controls the shorter term impact of smoking rate on smoking.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingpeakyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Peak year of smoking prevalence among adults aged over 30. When peak year is set to "on" prevalence begins to fall after specified year.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the rate of smoking among adults over the age of 30.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingstsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This switch turns on the 4 stages of smoking prevalence.

nodes.NAME: ssweltaxrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government taxes imposed on both households and firms for social security and welfare, expressed without units and by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase taxes and lower values decrease them.

nodes.NAME: edqualsecur
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of the impact of societal insecurity  on education quality score.

nodes.NAME: svdthsadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor on societal violence deaths.

nodes.NAME: svvionormsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for societal violence normalization. A value of 1 indicates on; 0 indicates off.

nodes.NAME: svtohlsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to activate linkage between societal violence and health. A value of 1 indicates on; 0 indicates off.

nodes.NAME: svindexm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on societal violence index From self-harm.

nodes.NAME: svmulm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on societal violence.

nodes.NAME: hlsolfuelsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the effect on respiratory diseases (and infections) when solid fuel use changes From the expected values.

nodes.NAME: ensolfueltrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to eliminate solid fuel use

nodes.NAME: ensolfueltrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the target value of percentage of people using solid fuel.

nodes.NAME: ensolflhldsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to hold the forecast of Solid Fuel Use at Base year levels

nodes.NAME: ensolfuelsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of Standard Errors to be targeted by the forecast (between -2 and 2), 0 turns off the targetting.

nodes.NAME: ensolfuelseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of years to target a given number of Standard Errors by the forecast.

nodes.NAME: edqualprispndimpthresholdval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Threshold value for threshold effect on spending impacts on primary education quality.

nodes.NAME: edqualsecspndimpthresholdval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Threshold value for threshold effect on spending impacts on secondary education quality.

nodes.NAME: edqualprispndimpthreshold
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A parameter to turn off/tune the impact of nearing threshold on the spending impacts on primary education quality.

nodes.NAME: edqualsecspndimpthreshold
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A parameter to turn off/tune the impact of nearing threshold on the spending impacts on secondary education quality.

nodes.NAME: hllongvtystartage
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the start age to apply Longevity Logistic Curve

nodes.NAME: sfmassrep
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for state failure mass repression. A value of 1 turns on totalitarian system-like repression that suppresses domestic conflict of any kind and value of 0 represents no such change (default case).

nodes.NAME: sfusehist
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to use history for base values of state failure. A value of 0 indicates off; 1 indicates on and 2 indicates convergence.

nodes.NAME: sfconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the convergence time of state failure to its expected value. Very often initial data values for countries will differ a little or much From values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

nodes.NAME: sfintlwarmagm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on state failure due to instability/internal war. This is a multiplicative factor that introduces a shift in the magnitude of internal conflict over time, for a country/region. It increases/decreases the index value (SFINTLWARALL) that the model computes.

nodes.NAME: sfcivilwarucdpsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: State failure/internal war UCDP switch .   When the swithc is 1 the variable SFCIVILWARUCDP will be connected to forward linkagess and parameters, otherwise variable SFINTLWARALL will be used.

nodes.NAME: sfintlwaradd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor to state failure/internal war measure. It introduces a shift in the  probability of internal conflict over time for a region/country.

nodes.NAME: HLSTUNT
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The percentage of the total population that is affected by childhood malnutrition

nodes.NAME: HLSTUNTCHL
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The percentage of children under 5 that is affected by childhood malnutrition

nodes.NAME: HLSTUNTWORK
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The percentage of the population in working age that is affected by childhood malnutrition

nodes.NAME: hlstuntchlm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the percentage of children under 5 affected by childhood malnutrition.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hlstuntyrs
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the moving average of stunting years.

nodes.NAME: survseadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor to introduce a shift in Survival/self-expression index for a region/country.  It increases or decreases the index value that the model calculates.  The normal value is zero.  See also and contrast with cultshmp, which is a cultural shift for the large cultural regions identified in the WVS project and which is calculated From data.

nodes.NAME: swseffmax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Swing State effects maximum annual magnitude (Polity points).  Because the Polity democracy scale runs From 1-10 (10=most democratic), you would normally not set a value for this parameter of more than 2-4 points, and most often it would be considerably lower.

nodes.NAME: swseffects
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Action-reaction switch.  A value of 1 (as in the base case) turns on an action-reaction dynamic in the determination of threat.  A value of 0 turns it off.

nodes.NAME: wpgreatlev
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, systemic power share required for full great power status.  The value is in percent of systemic power.  Thus 5.0 would indicate that a state reached the status of full great power when its share of total global power reached 5.0%.  See also the threshold for beginning to be a great power, wpgreatlev.

nodes.NAME: wpgreatthresh
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, systemic power share for threshhold great power status.  The value is in percent of systemic power.  Thus 2.0 would indicate that a state was just beginning to be a great power when its share of total global power reached 2.0%. See also the level to be a full great power, wpgreatlev.

nodes.NAME: hlmorbm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on initial morbidity to set a target for morbidity.  value of -1 is used as a switch to turn off the multiplier, otherwise used as a multiplier on initial morbidity.

nodes.NAME: TAXRA
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The tax rate.  This is no longer a parameter in IFs, but rather a variable computed in the first year.  For parameter control of taxes, see taxram.

nodes.NAME: taxinfadjm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on tax rate adjustments because of the extent of informal economy. A value of 0 specifies no adjustment; while a value of 1 specifies full adjustment.

nodes.NAME: etechadv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy technology advance rate (decrease in cost of energy production), expressed in decimal form (e.g. 0.01 equals 1 percent annual growth, by energy type).  Use, for example, to decrease the cost of renewable energy over time.  A value of 0.01 applied to renewable energy would force an annual decrease in the costs of producing solar energy of 1% each year, representing continued technological advance in such production (a value of -0.01 would represent a negative cost decrease, that is, a cost increase).

nodes.NAME: etechadvuncon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Unconventional energy technology advance rate (decrease in cost of energy production), expressed in decimal form (e.g. 0.01 equals 1 percent annual growth, by energy type).  Use, for example, to decrease the cost of renewable energy over time.  A value of 0.01 applied to renewable energy would force an annual decrease in the costs of producing solar energy of 1% each year, representing continued technological advance in such production (a value of -0.01 would represent a negative cost decrease, that is, a cost increase).

nodes.NAME: labcoeffsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on technology coefficients by sector and skill level.

nodes.NAME: infrateledtfp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for fixed telephone network divestment  time, number of years From peak. Peak is at 30% of mobile phone access.

nodes.NAME: envtemptoginidomel
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Gini Index to changes in temperature.

nodes.NAME: envtemptoginidomsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to turn on temperature to Gini Index impacts. A value of 0 indicates off; 1 sets it to U-shaped; 2 to elasticity; 3 to incremental U-shaped; 4 to absolute elasticity; 5 to Paglialunga and 6 to Paglialunga with average temperature.

nodes.NAME: termtrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on terms of trade.  The default value of this parameter is 1.0, signifying no exogenous shift in the terms of trade between more and less economically developed countries.  Relative prices in various sectors, particularly agriculture and energy, will still change endogenously.  A value greater than 1.0 additionally improves terms of trade for LDCs at the expense of developed countries.  A value of less than 1.0 shifts terms of trade to the benefit of wealthier countries.  A value of 1.2 would improve the terms of trade of the very least developed countries by about 20 percent.  This parameter should not normally be changed From 1 in the initial year.  Values should generally range From .5 to 1.5.

nodes.NAME: terdispute
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Territorial dispute or absence (1=dispute; 0=no dispute).  This is a dyadic value, between two countries or regions.  The user could change it From 1 to 0 at some point in time to indicate the resolution of dispute.  The initial values reflect actual disputes in the early 21st century.

nodes.NAME: edtergradgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, tertiary, graduation rate, annual additive growth. A parameter to make the countries meet education targets by an annual additive growth in the rate of graduation in tertiary level.

nodes.NAME: edtergndreqgrad
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education tertiary, no of years by which gender parity index for graduation rate reaches 1. The gender parity index is the ratio of the male rate to the female rate. Must set edgndreqsuron=1 for this to work.

nodes.NAME: edtergradtrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve 100% graduation rate in tertiary education.

nodes.NAME: edtergradm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Tertiary Graduation Rate Multiplier.

nodes.NAME: edterintgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, tertiary, intake rate, annual additive growth. A parameter to make the countries meet education targets by an annual additive growth in the rate of intake in tertiary level.

nodes.NAME: edtergndreqint
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education tertiary, no of years by which gender parity index for intake rate raeches 1. The gender parity index is the ratio of the male rate to the female rate.

nodes.NAME: edterintm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Tertiary Intake Rate Multiplier.

nodes.NAME: edterinttrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal intake rate in tertiary education.

nodes.NAME: edterscienshradd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, Tertiary, additive factor to change science and engineering share of total tertiary graduates (ex.: value of .1 takes share From 30% to 40%)

nodes.NAME: reac
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Reactivity (Actor, Target).  This parameter determines the magnitude of the threat felt by a target in response to changing power balances with respect to an actor.  A value of 1.5 means that the perceived threat shifts 50 percent faster than the power balance, while a value of .5 means that threat rises only 50 percent as fast.  The user should be aware, however, that in the calculation of how threat affects defense spending, reactivities to ALL actors will shape a country's/region's expenditures, thus often diffusing sensitivity to changes in power of only a single external actor.  By setting reac for all actors towards a target to 0.0, then focusing the attention of a target on a single actor (e.g. reac(Russia, China) = 1.0), you can eliminate that diffusion of attention.

nodes.NAME: wpthrconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, convergence time to predicted underlying threat levels.  Very often initial data values for countries, such as dyadic conflict in this case, will differ a little or much From values predicted by broader empirical analysis across states (and possibly across time).  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or idiosyncratic factors.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will very often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country- or dyad-specific "shift" should disappear.  A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.  It is possible to set this parameter to 1, thereby replacing the empirical value by predicted values already in the first year and then every year thereafter.

nodes.NAME: envclimsens
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that defines time sensitivity of how global temperatures change with the level of CO2 emissions.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingtcsel
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of TCS with smoking rates.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingtcs
nodes.Parameter Explanation: TCS is the weighted average of the list of 6 specific areas in which countries should work to reduce smoking, according to the tobacco control treaty.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingtcsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on tobacco control score. Used when the switch hlsmokingstsw is set to 1.

nodes.NAME: elasit
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of total domestic demand to stocks/inventories. Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: tfrconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: TFR (total fertility rate) convergence time to expected value.  Very often initial data values for countries will differ a little or much From values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

nodes.NAME: tfrmin
nodes.Parameter Explanation: TFR (total fertility rate) stabilization level with high income.  This is a very important parameter, because fertility rates in many developed countries have falled well below the 2.1 replacement level.  The level at which they stabilize for countries at the highest levels of income, and when they stabilize (you might change this over time), will greatly effect ultimate global population maximums and possible decline rates.

nodes.NAME: eltfrcon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of total fertility rate to contraception use.  For most model users, it is much easier to directly manipulate fertility (see tfrm).

nodes.NAME: tfrexovals
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Total Fertility Rate Exogenous Values (-100 is off)

nodes.NAME: tfrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Total Fertility Rate multiplier.  A multiplier on TFR, unitless, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase TFR (and ultimately increase population) and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: HLCOST
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The total cost of Health including 4 components, Morbidity, End of Life or Mortality, Life Extension, and Others.

nodes.NAME: HLEXPEND
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The total Health Expenditure includes 2 components, Public (GDS - Health) and private HLEXPENDPRIV

nodes.NAME: trademax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Maximum trade as a portion of tradable production base, expressed in decimal form. A value of 0.9 means 90%. Values can exceed 1.0 because some economies export and reexport more than they produce.

nodes.NAME: elastrpr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of trade with prices, by economic sector. A value of 1 implies a 1% increase in exports when local prices are 1% below world prices, and a similar increase in imports when local prices are 1% above world prices. Values generally range From 0 to 2 and remain constant over time. This parameter interacts with parameters elmpr1, elmpr2, elxpr1, and elxpr2, all of which play a role in the equilibrium-seeking structure of the economic/trade model.  Unfortunately, the collective meaning of these trade parameters in conventional elasticity terms is not as clear as it should be, because they have been set to assure market-clearing behavior.

nodes.NAME: tradsratadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor to introduce a shift in Traditional/rational-secular indexindex for a region/country.  It increases or decreases the index value that the model calculates.  The normal value is zero.  See also and contrast with cultshmp, which is a cultural shift for the large cultural regions identified in the WVS project and which is calculated From data.

nodes.NAME: hlvehsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch used to turn off the estimation of Smoking Impact, thus keeping the values constant after 2030. The GBD original forecast goes only until 2030.

nodes.NAME: deathtrpvsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the target standard errors for DEATHTRPV forecast. Value range between -2 to 2, with 0 indicating that the target is turned off. Used in combination with deathtrpvseyrtar.

nodes.NAME: deathtrpvseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies that number of years to reach the standard error target for DEATHTRPV.

nodes.NAME: wastewatertreatedm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on treated waster water.

nodes.NAME: tmortr2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Time-related reduction in mortality, in portion per year (i.e., .01 represents 1 percent). See and compare with tmortr; this represents catch-up in fertility reduction by poor countries using tech transfer.  Although time-related, it is obviously meant to represent the affect of technological advance on life expectancy.  This parameter is global, and you will often prefer to use mortm to introduce scenarios around mortality and life expectancy, because that parameter is country/region specific.

nodes.NAME: tmortr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Time-related reduction in mortality, in portion per year (i.e., .01 represents 1 percent).  Although time-related, it is obviously meant to represent the affect of technological advance on life expectancy.  This parameter is global, and you will often prefer to use mortm to introduce scenarios around mortality and life expectancy, because that parameter is country/region specific.

nodes.NAME: ttfrr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Time-related reduction in total fertility rate (TFR), in portion per year (i.e., .01 represents 1 percent).  Although time-related, it is obviously meant to represent the affect of technological and or cultural/value-based change in fertility rates.  This parameter is global, and you will often prefer to use tfrm to introduce scenarios around fertility rates, because that parameter is country/region specific.  This parameter represents, however, the historic phenomenon of "systemic shift" in fertility rates.

nodes.NAME: trucksm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on truck sales by country/region and truck type.  A value of 1.0 leaves truck sales unchanged.  An increase over time to 2.0 would approximately double truck sales of the specified type relative to the base case (total sales will be normalized and therefore unchanged relative to the base case).

nodes.NAME: truckstotm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on total truck sales by country/region.  A value of 1.0 leaves total sales unchanged.  An increase over time to 2.0 would approximately double total sales relative to the base case (sales by type will not always change proportionately, because of differing relationships with total sales).

nodes.NAME: trucksconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence time for truck sales in years. This value determines the number of years over which all countries/regions will converge to the chosen function (as determined by the switch, vehfuncsw) for the computation of truck sales per year.  A value of 1000 would effectively turn off convergence, so that initial country-specific variations From the function would be maintained over time.  A value of 60 would lead to near convergence by the middle of the 21st century.  Very rapid convergence seems improbable in the face of fundamental country differences in infrastructure, land area, culture, etc.

nodes.NAME: hlgbdconvUp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence time coefficient for bringing initial adjustments/normalization factors towards 1, upward convergence only

nodes.NAME: QEUNCON(Oil)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Capital output ratio for unconventional energy, in dollars, per barrel of production capacity, by region and energy category.  This variable determines how many dollars of capital are required in the production of a barrel of oil equivalent in each energy category.  It therefore represents the cost of energy production.  QEUNCON is exogenous only for nuclear and renewable energy.  Values for oil, gas, and coal are computed endogenously (and depend on remaining resources) and should be examined only as indicators.  To change the cost pattern for those energy forms, use resorm and increase or decrease resources.  Values for renewable and nuclear energy can be exogenously changed, but you should maintain the initial value of the base case.  A series of gradually lower costs could represent technological progress (e.g. in the solar component of renewable).  A series of gradually higher costs could represent the impact of environmental factors (e.g. increasing costs of nuclear waste disposal).  Higher or lower values will increase or decrease investment in a particular energy category and will affect its production level.  You should be aware that investment will respond only to changes over time in QE and not to changes in the initial condition.

nodes.NAME: labunemprm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on labor unemployment rate. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value.

nodes.NAME: labunemprtrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Long term unemployment rate target for labor market equilibration, used in conjunction with labunemprtrgtyr.

nodes.NAME: ictbroadtrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access to fixed broadband

nodes.NAME: watsafetrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access to safe water (through improved or household connection)

nodes.NAME: sanitationtrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access to sanitation (throughhousehold connection)

nodes.NAME: unpaidlaborm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on unpaid labor force. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: ldcropunusedshare
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the unused share of cropland.

nodes.NAME: edsecupprlen
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Duration of education, Upper secondary is the number of grades (years) in Upper secondary education, aggregation rule for group might result in non-integer values

nodes.NAME: edsecupprenrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier applied directly on upper secondary enrollment rate. Values greater (less) than 1 results in growth (decline) From the base level forecast when the multiplier value is 1. (Note: Transition and graduation rate parameters can also be used to bring in enrollment change. This parameter affects all but the first grade)

nodes.NAME: edsecupprgndreqgrad
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education upper sec, no of years by which gender parity index for graduation rate reaches 1. The gender parity index is the ratio of the male rate to the female rate. Must set edgndreqsuron=1 for this to work.

nodes.NAME: edsecupprgradgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, upper secondary (general), Graduation rate to the last grade, annual additive growth. A parameter to make the countries meet education targets by an annual additive growth in the survival rate in general upper secondary.

nodes.NAME: edsecupprgratrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve 100% Graduation rate From primary to upper secondary education.

nodes.NAME: edsecupprgram
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Upper Secondary Graduation Rate Multiplier.

nodes.NAME: edsecupprgndreqtran
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education upper sec, no of years by which gender parity index for transition rate raeches 1. The gender parity index is the ratio of the male rate to the female rate.

nodes.NAME: edsecupprtrangr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, upper secondary (general), transion rate From lower secondary, annual additive growth. A parameter to make the countries meet education targets by an annual additive growth in the rate of transition From general lower secondary to general upper secondary.

nodes.NAME: edsecupprtrantrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal transition rate From primary to upper secondary education.

nodes.NAME: edsecupprtranm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Upper Secondary Transition Rate Multiplier.

nodes.NAME: edsecupprvocadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, Upper Secondary, additive factor to change share of total vocational enrollment (ex.: value of .1 takes share From 30% to 40%)

nodes.NAME: vehicflpcm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on vehicles per capita by country/region.  A value of 1.0 leaves vehicles per capita unchanged.  An increase over time to 2.0 would double vehicles per capita relative to the base case.

nodes.NAME: vehfuncsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Vehicle function switch.  The switch controls which of several functions the model uses to compute car and truck sales.  The standard value for it is 4, which results in the use of a function for sales per capita dependent on GDP per capita at purchasing power, the WVS index for survival/self-expression values, and the WVS index for traditional/secular-rational values.

nodes.NAME: wagnerc
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Wagner's law coeficient; annual growth in govt expenditures.  Wagner's Law (From the late 1800s) said that government expenditures would continue to increase as a portion of GDP.  Although this effect must ultimately saturate (the model limits it), it has continued into the 21st century.  You can set a value in terms of annual percentage increase (or decrease) in government/GDP. Thus, 1 = 1% annual increase in the ratio.

nodes.NAME: waron
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A switch that can be used to turn on or off the possibility of war.  A value of 0 turns off war and a value of 1 makes it possible.  It does not, however, make war certain - that will depend on calculations within each dyad of the probability of war and the conversion (via random processes) of such probabilities into actual conventional or nuclear war.

nodes.NAME: wastewaterportiontreated
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the portion of treated waste water.

nodes.NAME: watwastetreatsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of Standard Errors to be targeted by the forecast (between -2 and 2), 0 turns off the targetting.

nodes.NAME: wastewatportreatreusedm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the portion of treated waste water that is then re-used.

nodes.NAME: watwastetreatcostm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for changing the cost of construction for a kilopmeter of unpaved road.

nodes.NAME: watwastetreatseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of years to target a given number of Standard Errors by the forecast.

nodes.NAME: watsafenewsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, water and Sanitation 5 Category Switch, 1 will use 5 category for infrastructure spending and forward linkage

nodes.NAME: watsafefwdsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, water and Sanitation 5 Category Switch, 1 will use 5 category for forward linkage, 0 will use 3 category for forward linkage. This does not affect spending.

nodes.NAME: hlwatsansw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the effect on diarrheal diseases when access to water and sanitation changes From the expected values.

nodes.NAME: watsafeimpcostm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter to change the unit cost relative to the base case.

nodes.NAME: waterdemandm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on water demand.

nodes.NAME: watprid
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Responsiveness of water price to change in stock/inventory levels.

nodes.NAME: watprii
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Responsiveness of water price to stock/inventory levels.  watprii and watprid are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities), most of which normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: watpricetoylelas
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity that helps create a multiplier on yield by multiplying the ratio of change in water price relative to base water price and adding to 1.

nodes.NAME: landirareaequipelas
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of water price to land area equipped for irrigation

nodes.NAME: watdemandelas
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of water price to water demand.

nodes.NAME: watres
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Renewable water resources, expressed in cubic kilometers. This parameter is now purely informational, because IFs does not have a dynamic water model that uses it to constrain water use.

nodes.NAME: waterhhlifeboreholetubewell
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, safe water connections, borehole or tubewell, lifetime in years

nodes.NAME: waterhhlifedugwell
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, safe water connections, dugwell, lifetime in years

nodes.NAME: waterhhlifepiped
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, safe water connections, piped, lifetime in years

nodes.NAME: watsafeexovals
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Water Safety Exogenous Values (-100 is off)

nodes.NAME: waterhhm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for the percentage of people living with different levels of access to drinking water. Values greater than 1 raises access relative to the base case value for the same year. Values lower than 1 reduce access.

nodes.NAME: waterhhbasictrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Water services, at least basic, years From model base year to reach the target value stored in the parameter waterhhbasictrgtval. The year count starts From the initial year of the mdoel.

nodes.NAME: waterhhbasictrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Water services, at least basic, target value to be reached by a certain number (waterhhbasictrgtyr) of years starting From the model base year. Default value is 100.

nodes.NAME: waterbudgetprotec
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is for budget protection of water services spending. (1 = full protection, 0 is no protection) Values in between 0 and 1 indicates the share of demanded budget that will be set aside of the normalization process.

nodes.NAME: waterhhsafetrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Water Services, Safely Managed, years From model base year to reach the target value stored in the parameter waterhhsafetrgtval. The year count starts From the initial year of the mdoel.

nodes.NAME: waterhhsafetrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Water Services, Safely Managed,  target value to be reached by a certain number (waterhhsafetrgtyr) of years starting From the model base year. Default value is 100

nodes.NAME: waterhhcostlowershr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, water services, share of services using lower-cost service. Base case value is 50/50 when both lower and upper cost services are available

nodes.NAME: waterfilteredm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for the percentage of people of a certain type of water source who are served with filtered water

nodes.NAME: watertoyieldswitch
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to allow water to constrain agricultural yields.

nodes.NAME: WATUSEPC
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Water use per capita.  Regional or country-specific water use per capita in million cubic meters per year.  It is only meaningful to change this value for the first year of model computation, because thereafter it rises or falls with crop production (implicitly with irrigation).  It is of interest to compare total computed water use (WATUSE) with water resources (watres).

nodes.NAME: waterwithdrawalm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on water withdrawal.

nodes.NAME: fprihw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Historic (inertial delay) change in food prices. Values close to 1 imply very rapid adjustment and values near 0 imply little or no adjustment.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: mhwag
nodes.Parameter Explanation: iMport propensity, historical (inertial) delay in change.  Values near 1.0 imply very rapid adjustment and values near 0 imply little or no adjustment.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: eprohw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy profits, historic (inertial delay) in impact on investment.  Values near 1.0 imply very rapid adjustment and values near 0 imply little or no adjustment.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: mhw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Import propensity, historical (inertial) delay in change.  Values near 1.0 imply very rapid adjustment and values near 0 imply little or no adjustment.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: ehw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy historical weight factor for impact of prices on demand.  This parameter controls the speed at which changes in energy prices effect demand.  Values near 1.0 imply very rapid adjustment and values near 0 imply little or no adjustment.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: mbasehw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Import base, historical (inertial) delay in change.  Values near 1.0 imply complete historical inertia and values near 0 very rapid adjustment.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: xhw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Export propensity, inertial delay in change.  This parameter computes a moving average of export propensity.  A value of 0.7 would weight the historical or moving average by 0.7 and the newly computed value by 0.3 (1-0.7).

nodes.NAME: wpwghtpow
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, contribution of various components to power index.  This is a vector across all the allowable contributing variables in the calculation of state power.  Values of "1" turn on the contribution of a variable and values of "0" turn off the contribution.

nodes.NAME: DIPLOIGO
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Standarized Weighted Number of Intergovernmental Organizations that a country belongs in a given year

nodes.NAME: DIPLOTREATY
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Standarized Weighted Number of Treaties that a country has signed (1) or ratified (2) in a given year

nodes.NAME: govriskweight
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The Risk Index is a weigthed average of the contribution to risk of a set of aproximately 20 variables. Each variable can contribute From 0 to 1 depending on where its value sits in the Minimum to Maximum range. The weights can take any value.

nodes.NAME: exomerpppmatchsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Value of zero preserves GDPPOT in ifsEcoPPP; Other values force GDP to be used instead. This is a part of the two-run exogenous sceanrio workflow.

nodes.NAME: xworkremitinm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Worker Remittances Received.

nodes.NAME: xworkremitoutm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Worker Remittances Sent.

nodes.NAME: xwblnintr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World Bank Interest Rate.

nodes.NAME: xwbloanr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World Bank Loan Portfolio, Basic Annual Growth Rate.

nodes.NAME: xwblnrepr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World Bank Loan Repayment Rate/Time.

nodes.NAME: xwblneqr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World Bank loan to Equity Ratio.

nodes.NAME: xwbsectar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World Bank Sector Target, Shares in Percent.

nodes.NAME: xfdiwgrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Global Foreign Direct Investment.

nodes.NAME: wmigrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World migration rate multiplier.  This is a very useful parameter for increasing or decreasing migration rates globally, because it applies to all rates rather than just to those for a particular country or region (for control by country/region see migrater).  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying variable and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: wpextinterv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: External intervention forcing switch.  A value of 1 turns on the intervention in a country From another country (unspecified); it will affect internal conflict

nodes.NAME: wppowhhsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, power index switch, 1 means using POWERHH index to drive forward linkages, instead of the defaul POWER index.

nodes.NAME: wvsagesw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for World Value Survets aging.  The parameter controls the dynamics associated with the value orientation of cohorts in the model.  The standard value for it is 2, which results in the "aging" of value orientations.  That is, value orientation is calculated From GDP per capita only for the youngest cohort; all others carry their orientation forward in time.  Any other value for wvsagesw (the WVS aging switch) will result in use of the cohort-specific functions with GDP per capita.

nodes.NAME: democpolityseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter sets the number of years to a given standar error target of DEMOC.

nodes.NAME: edyrsagm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, Years of Education Multiplier

nodes.NAME: hltfragehalflife
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the number of years after which the total fertility halves.

nodes.NAME: mfpconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence of Multifactor Productivity Growth represents the time (in years) for productivity to converge to the global function.

nodes.NAME: TGRYL
nodes.Parameter Explanation: No longer used as a parameter, rather computed only.  See ylm and mfpadd.  The values are in decimal terms, so that a value of 0.001 would convey a rate of 1%.

nodes.NAME: YIELDINT
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Yield intensity measured as the ratio between the actual yield and potential yield. Also allows for calculating the yield gap, i.e. 1- yield intensity

nodes.NAME: ylexp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Agricultural yields' exponent controlling saturation speed represents a slowdown in the rate of yield increases as they approach the maximum (ylmax), ensuring a gradual, asymptotic approach to the yield ceiling.

nodes.NAME: ldrtripm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on number of trips recieved
